title: China, Togo to deepen cooperation
body: Premier Li Qiang stressed on Thursday that China stands ready to deepen cooperation with Togo in various fields to better serve the modernization drive of both countries, as the two countries issued a joint statement on building a China-Togo community with a shared future in the new era. Li made the remarks while meeting in Beijing with Faure Essozimna Gnassingbe, president of the Council of the Togolese Republic, who is on an eight-day official visit to China through Friday. Li held a welcoming ceremony for the West African leader at the Great Hall of the People. During their meeting after the ceremony, Li said that no matter how the international landscape evolves, China and Togo should be good brothers and good partners that trust each other, carry forward their traditional friendship and cement political mutual trust. Li said that China is willing to work with Togo to further align development strategies, cultivate more growth drivers for cooperation, and strengthen collaboration in connectivity, infrastructure, agricultural modernization, finance and other fields, in order to boost their development momentum. China stands ready to import more quality products from Togo, and welcomes Togo to make full use of China's zero-tariff treatment and the upgraded green lanes for Togolese products exported to China, Li said. Gnassingbe said that China's rapid development has set an example for the world, and expressed his country's readiness to strengthen practical cooperation in various fields to improve the well-being of the two peoples. Togo supports resolving differences and addressing hotspot issues in Africa through dialogue, and is set to strengthen multilateral coordination with China to safeguard regional peace and stability, he added. After the talks, the two leaders witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents covering areas including industrial and supply chains, human resources, customs inspection and quarantine, and media collaboration. In a separate meeting on Thursday with Botswana's President Duma Gideon Boko, who is in Beijing for a state visit, Li said that in recent years, China-Botswana relations have maintained a sound momentum of development. Li expressed China's willingness to work with Botswana to pursue high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, better leverage their complementary economic strengths, make good use of mechanisms such as the joint commission on economy and trade, and deepen cooperation in areas such as mining, digital technology, green energy and artificial intelligence to achieve more tangible results. Boko said Botswana deeply admires China's development achievements, and highlighted that the elevation of bilateral relations to a comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership is a milestone. Botswana will leverage China's zero-tariff treatment, expand its trade with China, and further strengthen practical cooperation, he added. Liu Qinghai, a researcher at Zhejiang Normal University's Institute of African Studies, said the two high-level visits and the upgrading of both bilateral relationships are more than mere statements of friendship. Rather, these moves have laid a solid political foundation for subsequent cooperation, she added. Liu noted that the high-level talks have consistently highlighted zero-tariff treatment, green lanes, the vision of a shared future and core principles for collaboration.

title: Chinese desert fighter honored by FAO
body: Three Chinese women, including Yin Yuzhen, who has devoted more than four decades to combating desertification in northern China, were among 100 women heroes in agrifood systems and rural development honored by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations in Rome, Italy, on Thursday. "This prize doesn't belong to me alone," said Yin upon receiving the award from Qu Dongyu, director-general of the FAO. Yin added that the award also honored the "efforts of countless brothers and sisters that supported us". Over the past four decades, about 46 square kilometers of sandy land around Yin's home in Uxin Banner of Ordos in the Inner Mongolia autonomous region has been rehabilitated, with over eight million trees planted through efforts involving Yin, her family, local communities and government support, according to China's National Forestry and Grassland Administration. The other two Chinese honorees were Dong Minfang from Hunan province, who promotes mechanized farming and supports rural women through agricultural cooperatives, and Yu Jinxiu from Hubei province, who has trained over 30,000 practitioners of moxibustion therapy, helping to preserve traditional skills and create rural jobs. In May 2024, the UN General Assembly designated 2026 as the International Year of the Woman Farmer, aiming to recognize women's contributions to agrifood systems and to address persistent inequalities in access to land, finance, technology and decision-making. As part of the initiative, the FAO launched a program to honor women whose work has made a difference in agriculture, environmental protection and rural communities. A special guest at the Rome ceremony was Ronald Sakolsky, a retired history teacher from the United States who was moved by Yin's efforts and raised $5,000 to support her tree-planting efforts in the late 1990s, thus beginning a friendship that has endured for about 27 years. "Everything she gets, Ms Yin, she deserves," Sakolsky told China Daily. "She has worked very, very hard to take care of Mother Earth and to prove that the impossible is possible." Their friendship attracted international attention after President Xi Jinping recounted their story during his remarks at a state dinner hosted by US President Donald Trump at the White House in Washington, DC, on Sept 24. Xi said their story touches the hearts of many Chinese people and stands as a shining example of the friendly exchanges between the two peoples. Sakolsky also said that their friendship demonstrated the potential for closer people-to-people ties between the two countries. "Ms Yin and I are showing the world that Chinese and Americans can get along, but we are only two people and I hope other people want to be like us," he said. "We live on one Earth. It is not a Chinese Earth or an American Earth. It is only one Earth ... so for the sake of mankind, we must find a way to get along. We don't have to be best friends. We just need to be friends."

title: Brands need more than quality goods to go global, forum says
body: Chinese companies are increasingly establishing themselves as global brands, but their long-term international success will depend not only on technological innovation and competitive products, but also on their ability to engage consumers, forge emotional connections, and adapt to local markets, business leaders and experts said at a forum in London on Wednesday. The third Brand Finance China Brand Forum, held at Mansion House in the City of London, brought together business leaders and industry experts to explore the opportunities and challenges facing Chinese brands expanding internationally. Under the theme Sunrise in the East: Chinese Brands Going Global, speakers highlighted the growing recognition of Chinese companies across industries ranging from electric vehicles and consumer electronics to entertainment and digital platforms. Li Liyan, minister counselor at China's Embassy in the United Kingdom, said Chinese modernization provides a solid foundation for domestic brands to expand internationally, while the country's rich cultural heritage gives them a distinctive identity. "As Chinese brands go global, they showcase not only the achievements of Chinese manufacturing and innovation, but also the Chinese people's efforts to build better lives," he said. Li emphasized that successful international branding also requires greater cultural understanding and exchanges between countries. "Through dialogue, we can reduce prejudice. Through mutual learning, we can enrich our respective cultures," he said, adding that China and the UK have considerable potential to deepen cooperation in culture, business, and tourism. David Haigh, chairman and CEO of Brand Finance, said Chinese brands had made remarkable progress in international recognition in recent years, reflecting the country's growing competitiveness in technology and manufacturing. Recalling the forum's first edition three years ago, Haigh said many Chinese brands that were relatively unfamiliar to British consumers had since become increasingly recognizable. "I personally feel that … interaction with Chinese brands ... is much stronger than it was a few years ago," he said, adding that the trend was accelerating. He identified electronics, automobiles, and digital platforms as particularly promising sectors for Chinese brands, and pointed to the rapid international expansion of electric vehicle manufacturer BYD and social media platform TikTok. However, Haigh cautioned that producing high-quality goods was only part of the challenge. Chinese companies also need people with a deeper understanding of overseas markets, including local business practices and distribution networks. Michael Mainelli, a former lord mayor of the City of London and chairman of Z/Yen Group, emphasized that building a successful international brand required more than simply winning consumer recognition. "The global brand challenge is not simply to be understood; it is to be understood correctly," he said. Brands, he explained, help consumers navigate uncertainty by conveying information about quality, identity, expectations, and accountability. For Chinese businesses expanding overseas, success therefore requires understanding local cultures and expectations while consistently delivering on their promises. "A brand must be recognizable, relevant, and reliable," Mainelli said. The importance of communicating technological advantages was highlighted by Bono Ge, country manager for the UK and Ireland at BYD. Ge said Chinese automakers had developed sophisticated technologies, but consumers did not always fully understand or appreciate the features available in their vehicles. "I think what we did right is storytelling," he said, stressing the importance of helping customers experience and understand technology rather than simply presenting technical specifications. He added that building a premium brand requires something beyond functionality and competitive pricing. "In order to build a brand, you must create an emotional connection with brands," he said. For Chinese companies seeking to compete in Europe's established premium automotive market, technological innovation must therefore be accompanied by a distinctive brand identity and stronger consumer engagement. A similar message emerged from Afiah Kofie, who oversees public relations and communications in Europe for Chinese collectible toy company Pop Mart. Kofie said the company's international appeal was closely linked to storytelling around its intellectual properties and the artists behind them. Through exhibitions, events, and social media, Pop Mart seeks to introduce consumers to the characters and creative worlds behind its products, while cultivating communities of enthusiastic followers. She also highlighted artificial intelligence as an increasingly important channel through which consumers discover brands, making a compelling and accessible brand story essential. Looking ahead, Kofie identified beauty products as another promising sector for Chinese companies seeking international growth, particularly through social media and consumer advocacy.

title: Ukrainian on trial in Germany over Nord Stream blasts
body: A former Ukrainian military officer is facing trial in Germany, charged with masterminding the covert 2022 attack on the Nord Stream pipelines that severed Western Europe's main conduit for Russian natural gas. Serhii Kuznetsov appeared on Wednesday before Hamburg's Higher Regional Court, where his defense sought dismissal of war crimes and sabotage charges in proceedings expected to run into February. Four years after explosions ruptured the Baltic Sea pipelines, prosecutors allege that Kuznetsov commanded a dive team that planted charges on the seabed under orders from Ukrainian state authorities. Ukraine denies any state involvement. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said in August that his country had never officially taken part in operations targeting the pipelines. Prosecutors told the court the former special forces officer had committed a war crime by targeting civilian infrastructure, and has charged him with causing the explosions, destroying property, and disrupting essential services. The trial is politically sensitive in Germany, one of Kyiv's closest allies since the Russia-Ukraine conflict escalated in February 2022 — seven months before the pipeline explosions. The proceedings mark the first time evidence from the multiyear investigation has been aired in open court. Kuznetsov, who was extradited to Germany last year, denies the charges. He was arrested while on a family holiday in Italy, with prosecutors alleging he had been traveling on a false passport. A second suspect, Volodymyr Zhuravlyov, an air-conditioning installer and amateur diver, was arrested in northern Croatia in August on a European warrant. He has applied for asylum there and is fighting extradition to Germany, denying any role in the attack. Defense lawyers countered that investigators have gathered only circumstantial evidence in the years since the blasts. "(Prosecutors) made a thorough investigation of four years," Italian defense lawyer Nicola Canestrini told reporters outside the courtroom. "They did not find one single witness, they did not find no forensics, no DNA, no fingerprints — nothing!" Prosecutors allege Kuznetsov coordinated six accomplices — divers, an explosives specialist, and a ship's captain — who used a rented yacht to plant timer-controlled charges at around 80 meters depth in the Baltic Sea, near the Danish island of Bornholm. The explosions on Sept 26, 2022 ruptured the Nord Stream 1 pipeline carrying Russian gas to Germany. They also damaged the Nord Stream 2 pipeline, which had never been put into operation after Germany suspended the multibillion dollar project prior to the start of the conflict. Lawyers for Kuznetsov also argued the case should be dismissed, saying their client had spent 11 months in near-total solitary confinement and was being treated "like a pawn on a chessboard".

title: Do differences cause conflict? Confucius disagrees
body: Many have argued that in the contest among civilizational narratives unfolding in the first quarter of the 21st century, Samuel Huntington's thesis of the "clash of civilizations" proved "fitter" than Francis Fukuyama's "end of history" claim. The cutting edge of Huntington's argument lay in the assertion that following the Soviet Union's collapse in 1991, the conflicts of the future would be generated, for the most part, not by ideological, economic, or geopolitical contradictions of interest, but by civilizational differences. The very fact that Huntington used the word "civilization" in the plural is significant. It challenges the Western tendency to treat "civilization" as singular and synonymous with the West. Huntington's idea can be traced to the Calvinist influence in the American project, dating back to the Puritan 17th century, which promulgated the thesis of "election based upon double predestination". Its modern secular iteration is the myth of "American exceptionalism". To illustrate the Western inability to come to terms with the civilizational "other", I recall an old Zoroastrian creation story from the Bundahišn. This ancient Iranian religion is dualistic, since, unlike many other religious traditions, it postulates two uncreated metaphysical principles: the Good One — Ahura Mazda — or God, and the Evil One — Angra Mainyu or the Devil. There is an intriguing asymmetry between these two powers. Ahura Mazda is eternally aware of the existence of Angra Mainyu. However, Angra Mainyu only becomes aware of anything beyond himself upon the creation of the world. When Ahura Mazda creates the world, Angra Mainyu encounters something other than himself for the first time. His response is destruction: he seeks to eliminate this "other" and the world it represents. This story has a profound ethical lesson: Evil is characterized by an inability to accept the existence of anything different from itself, thus equating the very fact of difference with inevitable conflict. This analogy partly explains why being seen as "Number 1" matters so much to some nations. But their "Number 1" status seems to exclude the existence of "Number 2" or "Number 3". In a race, the fastest runner finishes first, a slower runner ends up second, someone still slower finishes third, and so on. All runners share the quality of "speed" and the difference is only one of degree. This is precisely what can get overlooked when international relations are viewed primarily in terms of mutually exclusive binary oppositions. Some are convinced that their political, economic and social arrangements are not just the best but the only viable options, dismissing alternatives. This reminds one of an old joke: "What is the definition of a Puritan? Someone who cannot stand the thought of someone, somewhere, having fun. "A modern version of the joke would be: "What is the definition of a certain type of Western public figure? Someone who cannot stand the thought of someone, somewhere, having an alternative." But, alternatives do exist. Writing from Qufu, Shandong province, the birthplace of Confucius, I reflected on his teachings at this year's Nishan Forum on World Civilizations. What might Confucius have said about the implications of civilizational differences? Do they inevitably mean conflict, as Huntington would have us believe? Difference is a necessary, though not sufficient, condition for conflict; Confucius, however, believed that it is also a precondition for harmony. His concept from the Analects — of "being harmonious but not uniform" — suggests that harmony can emerge from the coexistence of different entities, resolving tensions without erasing their fundamental differences. A beautiful melody must consist of different notes. Their collapse into a single note would destroy the very beauty that harmony engenders. Similarly, different civilizations could make the planet harmonious by remaining different. Is this an unrealistic ideal? Perhaps. Conflict, as noted above, requires difference. However, the existence of differences should not by itself cause conflict. Some politicians love to shout: "Choose a side!" The choice before us is whether to use our civilizational differences to build harmony or to abuse them as excuses for conflict. The author is a Sinologist, chair scholar at the Macedonian Academy of Sciences and Arts. The views do not necessarily reflect those of China Daily.

title: Yulin's blueprint for greening the desert
body: On Sept 2, 2026, I joined the International Seminar on Desertification Prevention and Sustainable Development Audit in Yulin, Shaanxi province. Hosted by the National Audit Office of China, or CNAO, the seminar showed that desertification is not only an environmental issue, but also a challenge to development and public governance. In his keynote address, Hou Kai, auditor-general of the CNAO, described desertification prevention as China's strategic choice. The message was clear: a problem of this scale cannot be solved by occasional projects, but requires a long-term national strategy. China does not see deserts simply as "problem areas". Instead, it seeks to transform ecological constraints into opportunities for sustainable development through the idea of "greenery advancing as deserts retreat". This is why Yulin is such an interesting case. The city shows how ecological restoration, water management, long-term planning and economic development can be combined in one development model. Yulin's lesson is that becoming "green" does not simply mean planting more trees. It means designing development in ways that fit the ecological conditions of the area. China emphasizes three important principles: a systematic approach, ecological priority and top-level design. In simple terms, this means looking at the whole system, respecting ecological limits and maintaining policy coherence from the national to the local level. Water is one of the most important constraints to dryland restoration. The CNAO therefore highlighted the idea of "Green Policies Tailored to Water Availability", reminding us that environmental policy must respect the carrying capacity of local water resources. This is where the role of supreme audit institutions becomes particularly important. Auditors should ask not only whether public money was spent correctly, but also whether that spending actually improved ecological conditions. Hou Kai summarized the CNAO's broader perspective with the idea that "national audit empowers desertification prevention and sustainable development". Another important approach is research-based auditing. Auditors are expected to understand the causes of problems, rather than relying only on checklists or formal compliance. If a restoration project fails, the question should not stop at whether the target was missed. Auditors should investigate whether the real cause was water scarcity, unsuitable vegetation, weak policy design, inconsistent funding or poor coordination. The CNAO also emphasizes performance auditing that tracks funds and project outcomes. This means following the connection between public expenditure and actual changes in vegetation, land use, biodiversity and other ecological conditions. Technology is becoming increasingly important in this work. Geographic information systems, remote sensing, drones, data analytics and AI allow auditors to examine large areas more efficiently and target field inspections more precisely. The cases presented by the CNAO, including the Great Bend of the Yellow River, Horqin and Hunshandake sandy lands, and areas around the Taklimakan Desert, reflect an ecosystem approach. Water, forests, soil, biodiversity, projects and funding must be examined together because environmental systems do not follow administrative boundaries. One particularly admirable point is that the CNAO did not present China's experience only as a success story. It openly identified continuing challenges such as regional disparities, inconsistent policy and funding support, and weak post-project maintenance. For me, Yulin is important not because it has simply "defeated the desert". It shows how a city can live within ecological constraints and gradually transform those constraints into drivers of sustainable development. The broader lesson from Yulin and the CNAO is that public auditing is moving from money to outcomes, from projects to systems, and from compliance to sustainability. From desertification to restoration, and from restoration to sustainable development, Yulin and the CNAO together offer a valuable model for environmental governance and environmental auditing. The author is deputy auditor-general of the State Audit Office of Thailand. The views do not necessarily reflect those of China Daily.

title: Asia-Pacific urged to ready workers for AI
body: The technological boom that has kept Asia-Pacific resilient amid external shocks has also exposed the vulnerabilities in the region's labor sector, the International Monetary Fund said on Thursday. The IMF's "Regional Economic Outlook: Asia and Pacific" report, launched at the annual meetings of the IMF and the World Bank in Bangkok, forecasts regional growth at 4.8 percent, supported by strong global demand for semiconductors and AI infrastructure. However, the annual report also noted that over the long term, AI could amplify underemployment and skills mismatches. "AI is reshaping occupations and the demand for skills for those roles," the report said, highlighting the need for policymakers across the region to promote the creation of high-quality jobs, support workers in acquiring relevant skills and facilitate labor mobility. Krishna Srinivasan, director of the IMF's Asia and Pacific department, said addressing youth unemployment and skills mismatches while supporting AI adoption is among the structural reforms the region needs to implement. There has been "a negative effect" on hiring in jobs more exposed to AI, with employer demand down 10 percent, he said. "But we also find that this has stabilized — even as AI capability has increased — suggesting that AI is reshaping work more than eliminating it, as employers are demanding workers who have AI skills," Srinivasan said at a news briefing held during the launch of the regional economic outlook. While the Asia-Pacific has benefited from AI exports and investments, "there is heterogeneity in terms of impact (on individual countries)", Srinivasan said. He cited the IMF's AI Preparedness Index, which assesses the level of AI preparedness of each country by looking at its digital infrastructure, human capital and labor market policies, innovation and economic integration, and regulation and ethics. For members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, Srinivasan said it is important to focus on harnessing human capital — through upskilling the labor force and ensuring the education system supports lifelong learning. ASEAN is one of the key beneficiaries of the AI boom as countries such as Malaysia and Singapore are deeply embedded in the global AI supply chain. Srinivasan said the IMF encourages policymakers across the region not just to adopt AI, but also to promote AI diffusion, which would spread the benefits across industries and across sectors of the population. Sonali Jain-Chandra, deputy director of the IMF's Asia and Pacific department, highlighted how a correction in the global AI market could hurt the economic outlook of South Korea — a key exporter of semiconductors and another major beneficiary of the AI boom. "There's a growing concentration of economic and financial market activity in (South Korea's) technology sector, and this could heighten vulnerability if there is a correction in global AI demand," she said. A reversal of the AI boom would dampen export revenues and investments and tighten financial conditions, she said. "But if AI diffuses across (different) sectors, if productivity gains are reaped, then there are upsides to the economy," she said. Releasing the regional outlook, the IMF also projected that India will become the world's fourth-largest economy by next year, overtaking Japan. Japan would remain the fourth-largest country by nominal GDP this year, but in 2027 India is set to take its place, with a GDP reaching $4.52 trillion. Japan is slated to slip to sixth place that year, falling behind both India and the United Kingdom, the projection showed.

title: 33 dead as roof of private school collapses in Pakistan
body: ISLAMABAD — At least 32 schoolchildren and one teacher were killed on Thursday when the roof of a school collapsed during morning classes in the northwestern Pakistani city of Peshawar, police and rescue officials said. Rescue workers spent hours pulling children from the rubble of the privately run Al-Khair Education Center, while panicked parents and relatives gathered outside the building seeking news of their loved ones. Most of the students killed were under 13. At least 45 people suffered major and minor injuries, said Arif Khattak, regional director of the Rescue Department. Television footage showed rescuers clawing through debris with their bare hands and carrying bloodied children to waiting ambulances as relatives and residents crowded the narrow alley where the school stood. A higher-floor roof collapsed onto students in classrooms below, crumpling two stories of the building, a rescue official said. "The fatalities include 12 girl students and a female teacher," Lady Reading Hospital spokesman Mohammad Asim said. Three children were in critical condition, with head injuries, Asim said, adding that most of the 20 injured brought to that hospital had been treated and sent home. The incident took place at 8:48 am, and the rescue operation lasted for four to five hours, Khattak said. "It was a weak building structure," Peshawar police chief Mian Saeed Ahmed said. "Its roof was overloaded with construction on a weak structure, which caused the collapse." Saeed said the school's owner had been arrested and that authorities had opened an investigation. Distraught relatives accused the school of ignoring concerns about the building's condition and demanded accountability. "Make an example of them, a lesson for all, so that no one dares open a school just to make money without providing facilities," said Mohammad Zaman, who lost his two nephews in the collapse. Earlier, police chief Saeed said he feared the death toll could rise as just 47 of the 110 students in three classrooms at the time had been rescued. There was no immediate comment from school officials. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed sorrow over the tragedy and offered condolences to the victims' families, according to a statement from his office. Roof and building collapses are common in the South Asian nation of more than 240 million people. In June, more than a dozen children were killed in a roof collapse at a tutoring center in the eastern city of Lahore.

title: Asia-Pacific projected to further strengthen role as key driver of global economic growth
body: The Asia-Pacific could further consolidate its position as a key engine of global economic growth by 2050, with its real gross domestic product projected to reach $140.24 trillion, according to a report released by a Chinese think tank on Sunday. The report, titled "Shaping Asia-Pacific 2050 Together: Building an Asia-Pacific Community and China's Future", was released by the Chongyang Institute for Financial Studies at Renmin University of China during the 2026 Tongzhou Global Development Forum in Beijing. Hosted by the university, the forum was held under the theme "China's Development and the Asia-Pacific Community", bringing together international participants to discuss regional cooperation and global development. The 21 member economies of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation generated $61.4 trillion in real GDP in 2025, accounting for 61.6 percent of the global total, according to APEC statistics. The report projected that the region's per capita real GDP could reach $48,000 by 2050, driven by advances in artificial intelligence, advanced manufacturing, renewable energy and life sciences. Regional trade in goods and commercial services could reach about $67 trillion by 2050, while trade in digitally delivered services is projected to reach between $16 trillion and $17 trillion, the report said. Research and development spending across the region could rise to between $6 trillion and $6.3 trillion, accounting for 4.3 percent to 4.5 percent of GDP by 2050. The report highlighted China's role in regional development, citing its vast consumer market, manufacturing capabilities and technological innovation as drivers of deeper economic integration and more resilient supply chains. It called for stronger regional cooperation in trade and investment, financial connectivity, digital governance, technological innovation and green development. The report also urged Asia-Pacific economies to strengthen coordination on long-term development priorities, improve cross-border payment systems and expand cooperation on artificial intelligence governance and sustainable growth.

title: Global experts hail BRI as critical bridge amid geopolitical turbulence
body: Political leaders and scholars have lauded the Belt and Road Initiative as an important platform for fostering inter-national connections in a world increasingly characterized by rising conflicts, fragmentation and protectionism. They made the remarks at the Wenzhou Business Development Forum — Zhejiang Belt and Road Think Tank Dialogue in Wenzhou city, Zhejiang province, on Saturday. Mulatu Teshome, former president of Ethiopia, offered his country's experience as a testament to the benefits that the BRI has brought to participating nations. Ethiopia and China signed a memorandum of understanding to promote cooperation under the BRI framework in 2018. The initiative has since delivered numerous cooperation opportunities to Ethiopia in infrastructure and trade investment, Teshome said, citing the Addis Ababa-Djibouti Railway as a prime example. The railway, Africa's first electrified trans-boundary rail line, entered operation in 2018 and has greatly reduced travel time between Ethiopia and Djibouti. The improvement in connectivity has also significantly boosted the flow of people and business opportunities, Teshome added, noting that many Chinese enterprises have built industrial parks along the railway. Jennifer Shipley, former prime minister of New Zealand, reflected on the evolution of the BRI. She observed that in the BRI's early stages, projects were primarily government-driven, focusing on infrastructure construction and financing, with the goal of promoting peace and prosperity through market connections. "Because we know that when people are connected to markets, peace and prosperity are most likely to nurture and flourish. And when it does nurture and flourish, there is mutual benefit to those economies," she said. As the initiative develops, the private sector is increasingly playing a crucial role in its implementation, she said. Official data reveal that in 2025, bilateral trade with BRI partner countries reached 23.6 trillion yuan ($3.52 trillion), increasing by 6.3 percent year-on-year and accounting for 51.9 percent of the country's total foreign trade value. Shipley said the BRI has created room for enterprises to conduct business, providing an important platform for companies navigating global chaos and waves of protectionism. Glenn Diesen, a professor at the University of South-Eastern Norway in Norway, emphasized the revolutionary role the BRI has played in connecting the Eurasian continent. Diesen described the initiative as a geographical revolution aimed at restoring physical connectivity across Eurasia. Following the implementation of the BRI proposed by China, countries such as Russia and Kazakhstan have also started similar initiatives to advance connectivity, but these initiatives are not exclusive and can mutually reinforce each other, he said. "With the physical connectivity of the Belt and Road Initiative, it enables more technological cooperation between the different centers of power," Diesen stated. "Overall, this international economic architecture lays the foundation for a new multipolar system. And in this multipolar system, we see that genuine multilateralism actually has a possibility to thrive … allowing economic connectivity to actually lead to peace." The 2026 Wenzhou Business Development Forum — Zhejiang Belt and Road Think Tank Dialogue is part of the Mingde Strategic Dialogue 2026 activities, which brought together former government leaders, scholars, and think tank experts from seven countries. The forum was jointly hosted by Wenzhou Business College and Zhejiang Development and Planning Institute, with support from the Chongyang Institute for Finance Studies at Renmin University of China.

title: Pacific Island countries seek lasting gains from China ties
body: Political leaders from Pacific Island countries said China's engagement with the region has focused on supporting development rather than geopolitical competition, and expressed interest in deepening cooperation to strengthen local economies and improve people's livelihoods. At the sixth China-Pacific Island Countries Political Leadership Dialogue in Beijing on Saturday, delegates identified trade and investment, infrastructure, healthcare, education, climate action and marine protection as priorities for further cooperation. Tongan Deputy Prime Minister Viliami Uasike Latu, who led the visiting delegation, said ties with China had steadily strengthened, bringing benefits in areas including education, agriculture and climate resilience. He cited scholarships for Tongan students to study in China, Chinese technical assistance in agriculture and fisheries, and support for climate-resilient infrastructure as examples of the progress made. Latu said further cooperation should reflect the priorities of island countries themselves, helping businesses overcome barriers to international markets while strengthening local capacity to use and maintain new technologies. Such cooperation, he said, should create opportunities that people can see in their daily lives: "a business reaching a new market, a young person gaining a useful skill, or a community better prepared for a natural disaster." In May 2025, China announced $2 million in funding for climate cooperation with Pacific Island countries and pledged to implement 100 small-scale community projects over three years to strengthen climate resilience. Liu Haixing, head of the International Department of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said China stands ready to work with Pacific Island countries to explore new approaches to cooperation that enable developing nations to set their own agendas, make decisions through consultations on an equal footing and share development benefits. Such cooperation could provide practical examples for Global South countries seeking to address common challenges through solidarity and greater self-reliance, Liu said. He stressed that China respects the sovereignty and independence of Pacific Island countries and has never regarded the region as an arena for major-power rivalry. China is also willing to pursue trilateral and multilateral cooperation with other partners to promote regional peace, stability and prosperity, he said. Liu called for closer alignment between China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30) and the development strategies of Pacific Island countries, alongside deeper cooperation in trade, digital technology and green development. He also emphasized the role of political parties in advancing cooperation, calling for stronger strategic communication, exchanges on governance experience and practical collaboration through the "political parties plus" approach. Alatoi Ishmael Kalsakau, former prime minister of Vanuatu, described the dialogue as a new dimension to ties between China and Pacific Island countries, saying it was bringing the two sides closer together in pursuit of common interests and a shared future. He said ideas such as equal partnership and a shared future were increasingly taking shape in tangible developments. Citing China's achievements in poverty reduction and its engagement with other countries, he said he believed China was genuinely willing to help countries such as Vanuatu improve people's lives. Kalsakau also emphasized that each country should be able to pursue its own development path, describing China as an equal partner that respected the choices of others rather than seeking control. He said the dialogue had provided opportunities for Pacific representatives to discuss their priorities directly with Chinese officials, allowing the two sides to identify areas for further cooperation. "They listen to us," he said, emphasizing the importance of regular exchanges built on mutual respect. Morris Tovebae, general secretary of Papua New Guinea's ruling Pangu Pati, reaffirmed his party's commitment to the one-China principle, describing it as a foundation of bilateral relations as the two countries mark 50 years of diplomatic ties this year. He also highlighted the impact of 26 years of Juncao technology cooperation, saying it had improved livelihoods and contributed to his country's development. He said communities, including those on remote islands, had benefited from mushroom cultivation, with locally grown mushrooms now being sold in markets and supermarkets. Efforts were also underway to explore export opportunities, he added. Beyond economic cooperation, Tovebae was particularly enthusiastic about learning from China's experience in political party organization and governance. Having visited China about 17 times and witnessed its transformation, he said he had come to believe that the CPC's strong organizational system and leadership were central to the country's development achievements. Tovebae said he was eager "to learn how the party system works here", hoping to draw on that experience to advance reforms within Pangu Pati so that the party could better serve not only its members but the country as a whole.

title: New China-DPRK border bridge over Yalu River opens to traffic
body: SHENYANG -- The new China-DPRK Yalu River bridge officially opened to traffic on Thursday, with both sides jointly holding an opening ceremony on this cross-border artery. The cable-stayed bridge over the Yalu River serves as a cross-border transport link between the city of Dandong in Northeast China's Liaoning province and the city of Sinuiju in North Pyongan province in the Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK). The double-pylon and double-cable-plane bridge features a 28.5-meter-wide deck designed with four lanes for two-way traffic, while its water navigation clearance is designed for vessels of up to the 3,000-ton class. The new bridge will further facilitate trade and people-to-people exchanges between the two countries, Chinese foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said on Wednesday. China and the DPRK are friendly neighbors connected by mountains and rivers, and the new bridge is an important facility for connectivity between the two countries, Mao noted at a regular press briefing. Dandong boasts China's largest border trade port with the DPRK. Before the new road bridge, the Yalu River Bridge, also known as the China-DPRK Friendship Bridge, served as a combined road-rail bridge. The old one, however, could only accommodate trucks weighing no more than 20 tons for one-way road traffic. China and the DPRK in 2010 agreed to build a new road bridge downstream from the old one.

title: Flowing with AI's growth highlighted at skills event
body: Qiu Mengying, 25, is confident that her aircraft engineer job is indispensable and has no fear she will be replaced by intelligent machines. Despite heated debate over the threat to the workforce posed by artificial intelligence, Qiu, a member of an aircraft maintenance training team that participated in the recent 48th WorldSkills Competition, said: "In our profession, AI is just a helper. It is not here to replace us." The seven skills added to this year's event, which concluded in Shanghai on Sept 27, are unique and hard to automate, she added. "These new skills reflect the latest trends in occupational development and industrial upgrading," said Qiu, while demonstrating her aircraft maintenance skills at the China Eastern Airlines exhibition booth. "They send a signal to more students and young people about where career opportunities are headed, while helping them gain a clearer understanding of their own career plans." Unlike many standardized and repetitive jobs, the new skills included in the competition offered a glimpse of the expertise workers will need as industries transform and develop. Known as a bellwether of industrial upgrades and employment trends, WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 helped shed light on "irreplaceable occupations" despite AI's spread, said officials and participants. The skills look to tap into the core employment requirements of digitalization, multidisciplinary and specialized skills. They send clear signals that despite the overwhelming application of AI across various cutting-edge sectors — including digital economy, smart infrastructure and modern commerce — humans cannot be replaced by intelligent machines, the officials and participants said. "There are a total of 64 skills at this year's competition, including seven new skills appearing at the event for the first time," Wu Liduo, director general of occupational capacity building at the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, said during a State Council Information Office news conference in Beijing in June.

title: SPC bolsters IP rights of seed industry
body: China's top court has underscored the importance of strengthening intellectual property protection in the seed industry, emphasizing the appropriate application of punitive damages in infringement cases involving new plant varieties. The Supreme People's Court released five landmark cases involving new plant varieties on Wednesday, highlighting the need for strict penalties against serious infringements to protect seed rights, promote innovation and safeguard national food security. The cases involve major crops such as rice, wheat and corn, which are crucial to national food security, as well as fruit and vegetable varieties, including passion fruit and blueberries, that contribute to dietary diversity. The release came ahead of World Food Day, which falls on Oct 16 each year. In one case, a Spanish company holding plant variety rights for a blueberry variety authorized a Chinese company to manage and protect those rights in China. The Chinese company discovered that a planting base in Yunnan province was propagating and selling seedlings of the protected variety without authorization. Established in July 2024, the planting base began advertising blueberry seedlings on social media platforms, including WeChat and Douyin, posting images of its nursery facilities and seedlings. On July 30, 2024, the Chinese company purchased seedlings suspected of infringing the variety rights, with the transaction notarized to preserve evidence. Sales staff at the planting base referred to the variety as "Spanish 42" and acknowledged that it was being cultivated alongside other varieties. Of the 120,000 seedlings at the base, 20,000 belonged to the disputed variety. The base was unable to provide legal documentation authorizing its propagation. Subsequent testing confirmed that the seedlings were nearly identical to the variety protected by the Spanish company's rights. The Chinese company then filed a lawsuit with the Kunming Intermediate People's Court in Yunnan. The court found that the planting base had willfully infringed the plant variety rights by producing, propagating and selling the seedlings without permission. It also found that the base had propagated another variety without authorization, with more than 67 percent of its seedlings lacking legal provenance. The court therefore applied punitive damages and ordered the planting base to pay 144,000 yuan ($21,519) in compensation for economic losses, along with 10,000 yuan in enforcement costs. The planting base appealed to the SPC, which rejected the appeal and upheld the original judgment. The SPC said the application of punitive damages demonstrated the judiciary's firm stance against infringement and reflected Chinese courts' commitment to providing equal protection to litigants, regardless of whether they are domestic or foreign. The top court also stressed the need to establish a comprehensive judicial protection system covering the entire process, from breeding and seed production to propagation and sales. It called for continued improvements to the legal rules governing intellectual property rights in the seed industry, taking into account the seasonal nature of crop growth and differences in propagation methods. The SPC urged courts nationwide to handle disputes involving new plant varieties fairly and efficiently, pledging to foster a fair and orderly legal environment that supports innovation and helps safeguard national food security.

title: China deploys five teams for latest batch of environmental inspections
body: BEIJING -- Five central ecological and environmental protection inspection teams have completed their deployment for the seventh batch of the third round of inspections, the Ministry of Ecology and Environment said Thursday. The latest batch includes two regular inspection teams assigned to inspect government ministries and three special inspection teams focusing on pollution in caves, sinkholes and valleys. The two regular teams will conduct one-month inspections of the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development and the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs. A special team will carry out inspections in Hubei, Hunan and Guangxi, with a second team operating in Chongqing and Sichuan, and the third based in Guizhou and Yunnan. Their inspections are expected to last about two weeks. The ministry said the inspections aim to strengthen environmental protection accountability, accelerate the country's green transformation, substantially improve environmental quality, and achieve major progress in building a Beautiful China. Central ecological and environmental protection inspections are a major institutional arrangement introduced in 2015 to advance ecological civilization. Multiple batches of inspections have strengthened accountability for local environmental protection and helped address long-standing problems in different regions. The current third round of inspections was launched in November 2023. China's landmark Ecological and Environmental Code officially came into force on Aug. 15, strengthening the legal foundation for ecological protection. Adopted by China's top legislature in March, the code is China's second formal statutory code after the Civil Code. The code comprises 1,242 articles in five chapters, covering pollution control, ecological protection, and green and low-carbon development, among other areas. The code also includes provisions on central ecological and environmental protection inspections.

title: Four additions take China's irrigation project sites on World Heritage List to 46
body: The Ministry of Water Resources announced on Thursday that four Chinese irrigation projects have been newly designated as World Heritage Irrigation Structures, bringing the country's total to 46. This designation was announced during the 77th International Executive Council Meeting of the International Commission on Irrigation and Drainage held in Marseille, France, on Wednesday. The newly recognized sites include the Guangli Canal in Henan province, the Taolai River Oasis Irrigation System in Gansu province, the Huangsha Canal in Jiangxi province and the Longjin ancient dam irrigation project in Fujian province. Each of these systems showcases unique historical and engineering significance, a media release from the ministry noted. The Guangli Canal, dating back more than 2,200 years to the Qin Dynasty (221-206 BC), is a large-scale irrigation system that continues to support agriculture in Jiyuan and Jiaozuo in Henan. Its innovative multihead diversion system and sediment separation techniques highlight ancient Chinese engineering prowess. The Taolai River Oasis Irrigation System, established during the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644), exemplifies the adaptation of irrigation techniques in arid regions, incorporating extensive tunnels and water distribution systems that sustain more than 63,187 hectares of farmland. In Jiangxi, the Huangsha Canal, originating in the Song Dynasty (960-1279), demonstrates a low-impact development model with its distributed tiered system of dikes and ponds, efficiently irrigating about 1,333 hectares of farmland and forest. The Longjin ancient dam in Fujian, with its origins in the Song Dynasty, employs a low-dam design that minimizes environmental disruption while maximizing water resource utilization for approximately 1,847 hectares of agricultural land.

title: Alpaca breeding a win-win for herders, grassland
body: Alpacas are helping herders protect grassland while increasing their incomes at one of China's largest alpaca breeding bases in Sonid Left Banner, Xiliin Gol League, Inner Mongolia autonomous region. The 280-hectare base belongs to Sonidalpaca, a company established in 2013 by Chi Haitao, a retired veteran turned entrepreneur. Chi started the venture with 78 high-quality alpacas imported from Australia. The animals initially struggled to adapt to the cold. "In the middle of winter, they shivered so hard that they could not stand up," Chi said. The base built warm sheds and studied disease prevention and breeding techniques. After eight years, all 78 alpacas had survived and adapted to the local grassland environment, he said. Large-scale breeding began in 2021. The base now raises 1,500 alpacas, generating a comprehensive output value of more than 5 million yuan ($747,000). In 2022, it was named an agricultural and animal husbandry science and technology demonstration park by Xiliin Gol League, Chi said. Alpacas offer multiple sources of income. Their fleece is among the high-quality animal fibers recognized by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations. According to Chi, alpaca fleece is four times warmer than ordinary wool, and processed fleece sells for more than 2,000 yuan per kilogram, earning it the nickname "soft gold". Alpaca meat is high in protein and low in cholesterol, making it a premium product in European and American markets, he said. Alpaca-derived nanobodies can also be used in medical research into treatments for human diseases. In addition, the animals can be raised as pets or used in tourism. An adult alpaca sells for about 30,000 yuan, Chi added. Chi, who is Han Chinese, has lived on the grassland for 13 years and has helped local ethnic Mongolian herders increase their incomes. Under a cooperation model involving gacha — a village-level administrative unit in the Mongolian language — and local herders, the company encourages herders to raise alpacas supplied by the business. It then buys back young alpacas for at least 10,000 yuan each and purchases fleece for at least 1,000 yuan per animal. "Raising 10 alpacas is equal to the income from raising 200 sheep," Chi said. All 500 young alpacas bred at the base this year have already been booked, he added. The initiative has also helped strengthen the local collective economy. "The alpaca industrial base has brought 390,000 yuan to our gacha's collective economy every year. We use the money to pay old-age insurance for herders, which has increased their sense of happiness," said Enkhbat, Communist Party of China secretary of Bayankhangai gacha. Beyond its economic benefits, alpaca breeding can help protect the grassland ecosystem. Alpacas consume about half as much as sheep, reducing pressure on pasture. They lack upper front teeth, so they nibble grass tops without pulling out the roots. Their padded feet also cause less damage to grassland, helping vegetation recover. "For example, 600 sheep may graze a patch of grassland bare, while the grassland after 600 alpacas feed can still maintain good growth," Chi said. Alpaca manure, meanwhile, is rich in nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium, which can improve soil fertility and structure and promote grass growth, supporting a more sustainable ecological cycle. The company plans to expand its operations gradually and encourage more local herders to participate in alpaca breeding, Chi said.

title: Claims of chemical in diapers disproved
body: Chinese authorities said on Thursday that a nationwide investigation had found no formamide in baby diapers, refuting online claims that the industrial chemical had been detected in the products. In late June, a media report said some consumers had reported recurrent diaper rash and skin ulceration in their babies after using certain brands of infant diapers. It also claimed that third-party tests had detected traces of formamide in several mainstream diaper products and that the chemical had been found in the blood and urine of some consumers. Following the report, several diaper brands, including Babycare, Huggies and BIBAbebe, said internal and external tests had found no traces of the chemical in their products. Disease control agencies conducted spot checks at all 168 baby diaper manufacturers operating in China, covering 368 batches of products from 180 brands. They also tested 32 batches of samples taken from key areas of diapers, including waistbands and fasteners. No formamide was detected, according to the investigation team jointly established in late June by the State Administration for Market Regulation, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, the National Health Commission and the National Disease Control and Prevention Administration. The team also retested remaining diaper samples provided by a social media blogger surnamed Wang, who had claimed to have detected formamide in the products. Tests conducted by three official professional testing institutions found no formamide in any of the 58 batches of products from 15 brands, according to the investigation results. Through exchanges with Wang, testing experts and industry insiders also identified multiple problems with his testing methods, undermining his conclusion that formamide had been detected. On-site inspections of all 168 manufacturers found that the companies met hygiene standards, with no evidence that formamide had been added to products or was present in their production processes or raw materials, the investigation team said. Authorities also investigated positive test results reported by two private testing institutions and an individual. They identified irregularities in the testing procedures, including the absence of blank and parallel sample tests and a failure to compare peak retention times with reference standards. The investigation team said the results of those tests were insufficient to conclude that formamide had been detected. Formamide is a colorless, water-soluble chemical used in industrial manufacturing and laboratory research. Exposure through inhalation, ingestion or skin absorption can harm human health, with particular concerns about its potential reproductive toxicity and effects on fetal development. The investigation team stressed that testing baby diapers for formamide requires professional expertise and rigorous procedures, while research into the chemical's health hazards must be conducted prudently and objectively. Health authorities in Shandong province have dealt with violations involving medical institutions and personnel identified during the investigation, the team said. Authorities will continue to strengthen oversight of infant products, guide manufacturers in improving their quality management systems and hold them accountable for product safety.

title: Chinese vice-premier discusses AI with Tsinghua SEM advisory board members
body: BEIJING -- Chinese Vice-Premier Ding Xuexiang met with representatives of the advisory board of the Tsinghua University School of Economics and Management (Tsinghua SEM) in Beijing on Tuesday. Ding, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, exchanged views with the representatives, focusing on the development and governance of artificial intelligence (AI). AI is a key force driving a new round of technological revolution and industrial transformation, Ding said, stressing the need to develop, apply and govern this future-shaping technology to better benefit all humanity. He welcomed the representatives' support for and participation in the development of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO), with a view to promoting shared prosperity and safeguarding common security. Noting that the advisory board has served as an important platform for dialogue, exchanges and cooperation between China and other countries over the past 26 years, Ding expressed hope that its members would make further contributions to China's education sector and economic development. The representatives, including Tim Cook, chairman of the advisory board, spoke highly of China's achievements in AI and other fields. They expressed their willingness to remain committed to the Chinese market, expand cooperation and better fulfill the board's role as a bridge between China and the international community. The Tsinghua SEM advisory board was founded in October 2000. Comprised of global business executives, business school deans and renowned scholars, the board aims to help make Tsinghua SEM a world-class school in terms of economics and management by improving its teaching and research capabilities.

title: Chinese vice-premier urges strengthening of advanced manufacturing
body: CHANGCHUN -- Chinese Vice-Premier Zhang Guoqing has called for strengthening and expanding advanced manufacturing, enhancing the self-reliance and controllability of industrial chains, and accelerating the building of a modern industrial system with advanced manufacturing as its backbone. Zhang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, made the remarks during his inspection tour in the northeastern province of Jilin from Thursday to Saturday. He stressed the need to make greater efforts to promote the deep integration of scientific and technological innovation with industrial innovation, encourage enterprises, especially large ones, to strengthen basic research, and achieve breakthroughs in a number of key core technologies and generic technologies. Efforts should be made to develop next-generation intelligent manufacturing, accelerate the widespread application of digital, intelligent and green technologies, and promote the renewal and upgrading of traditional industries, Zhang said. He also emphasized the need to strengthen basic theoretical studies on scientific research instruments and give full play to the role of key scientific and technological research forces, including national laboratories, national research institutions, high-level research universities and leading sci-tech enterprises. Zhang urged efforts to enhance common supporting capabilities for scientific research instruments, such as system integration, standards and metrology, pilot-scale verification, and inspection and testing, so as to promote the application and dissemination of independently developed technologies and products.

title: China unveils plan to expand, improve rehabilitation, nursing care services
body: BEIJING -- China on Thursday unveiled a plan to expand and improve medical rehabilitation and nursing care services, with measures to increase service resources, strengthen professional training and promote the use of artificial intelligence (AI). Under an implementation plan issued by the National Health Commission and the National Development and Reform Commission, cities with large populations, a rapidly aging population and growing demand for rehabilitation and nursing care services are expected to have at least one public rehabilitation hospital and one public nursing care facility by 2030. The plan also aims to provide about 0.48 rehabilitation and nursing care beds per 1,000 people, as well as 0.7 rehabilitation physicians and 1.6 rehabilitation therapists per 10,000 people, by 2030. To improve the service system, the plan calls for strengthening the rehabilitation and nursing care service network and enhancing the rehabilitation and nursing care functions of medical and healthcare institutions. The plan prioritizes support for cities at the prefecture level and above with more than 1 million urban residents in expanding and improving medical rehabilitation and nursing care services. It urges improvements to rehabilitation and nursing care disciplines and programs at universities and vocational colleges, including appropriately expanding enrollment and better aligning training with employment. Efforts will also focus on ensuring key departments, including intensive care, orthopedics and neurology, have medical professionals with specialized rehabilitation and nursing care skills. The plan highlights the use of AI in rehabilitation and nursing care services, encouraging the adoption of rehabilitation robots, smart wearable devices and other technologies to support the monitoring of multiple health indicators and provide intelligent rehabilitation training and health management services. In July, China's State Council unveiled a national health plan for the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-30), aiming to raise the country's average life expectancy to 80 years by 2030. It identifies expanding and improving rehabilitation and nursing care services as an important part of broader efforts to develop a high-quality, efficient and integrated healthcare service system.

title: China to revise train-numbering system as railway network expands
body: China will overhaul its train-numbering system to accommodate its expanding railway network and growing number of train services. The revised system will also leave room for new lines, equipment, and products, while reserving the X prefix for Fuxing trains with maximum operating speeds above 350 kilometers per hour. The changes will expand the number of available train numbers for passenger multiple-unit services by nearly 40 percent, according to China State Railway Group, the national railway operator. During peak travel periods, such as the May Day and National Day holidays, G-series trains — which account for most high-speed services in China — already use more than 90 percent of available G-series numbers, the operator said. For passengers, including international visitors, some familiar letters will take on new meanings. Previously used for conventional express and fast trains, T and K will designate multiple-unit trains with maximum operating speeds of 300 km/h and 200 to 250 km/h, respectively. G will designate Fuxing trains with a maximum operating speed of 350 km/h. The changes will be introduced in two stages, starting with regular-speed passenger trains, tourist trains, and some freight services in late November, followed by high-speed and other services in late December. The 12306 booking platform will display the new passenger train numbers within the 15-day advance booking window for the affected services. Travelers should check the updated train number, stations, and departure time for their travel date. Existing onboard services, including quiet carriages and online meal ordering, will remain available.

title: Tech innovations take spotlight at Canton Fair
body: Inside the Pazhou Complex, Leaw Cheeeyrn, a Malaysian businessman with high-level paraplegia, was able to walk with the assistance of a robotic exoskeletal device. "It was wonderful and I hope there will be more such high-tech products to help us walk," he said. He was accompanied by his wife at the China Import and Export Fair, which opened its 140th session in Guangzhou, capital of Guangdong province, on Thursday. At the event — also widely known as the Canton Fair — domestically produced high-tech products, especially artificial intelligence-driven electronic products and medical equipment, were highly favored by foreign buyers. The fair aligns with new trends in foreign trade, with 64 percent of the 32,000 participating companies utilizing new technologies such as AI and industrial internet, according to the organizers. The proportion of new and green products exhibited reached 23.2 percent and 26 percent, respectively, both setting records, the organizers said. China's manufacturing sector has been continuously transforming and upgrading, leading to an optimized foreign trade structure and a steady increase in the technological content of import and export products. Electronic components, industrial robots, 3D printers and new energy vehicles have performed exceptionally well, becoming new drivers of foreign trade momentum, the organizers said. "We are very interested in selling these products to Malaysia, where there will be high demand for intelligent robotic products," the Malaysian businessman said. The exoskeleton robotic device, developed by RoboCT — a Chinese company dedicated to the development and application of exoskeleton robotics — has been sold to more than 50 countries and regions. "We have developed intelligent products that help people with walking disabilities walk again and better," said Zhang Jiyu, co-founder and chief operating officer of RoboCT. On the fair's opening day, the company's exhibition booth attracted a large number of foreign buyers from the Middle East, Southeast Asia, Europe, Japan and South Korea. The company displayed its new rehabilitation service of mind-driven exoskeletons powered by brainwave signals and its GoGo-H Pro climbing series — a consumer-grade assistive exoskeleton for daily mobility. "We have brought a comprehensive product lineup covering medical rehabilitation, daily mobility assistance and industry support, aiming to showcase to our global partners the full-spectrum application capabilities of Chinese exoskeleton technology," Zhang said. The company, based in Hangzhou, capital of Zhejiang province, realized a year-on-year increase of 46.22 percent in overseas sales in 2025. In the first eight months of this year, its overseas sales increased about 149.76 percent year-on-year. At the fair's 139th session in April, the company — participating for the first time — successfully obtained the contact information of over 40 overseas distributors, with the total value of intended orders exceeding $3.5 million. "The fair is an important window for Chinese manufacturers to reach the world and a key milestone in our globalization strategy," said Zhang. The fair, seen as a barometer of China's foreign trade, runs in three phases from Oct 15 to Nov 4. Over the past 70 years, the fair has grown into China's largest and longest-running international trade event, with the most complete product range, the largest number of buyers and the highest transaction volume.

title: Wind power drives China's global green energy edge
body: China's rapidly expanding wind power sector has not only achieved leapfrog growth domestically, but has also emerged as a key driving force for the global clean energy transition, as the nation pivots toward high-quality development and reliable system substitution. The country established the world's largest wind energy industrial system during the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021-25), supported by the globe's most comprehensive supply chain. This robust foundation has provided substantial momentum and cost-effective equipment for worldwide renewable energy deployment, according to the National Energy Administration. In 2025, China's newly installed offshore wind capacity exceeded 7 million kilowatts, accounting for nearly 80 percent of the global total. The offshore wind industry is expected to maintain its growth momentum in the coming years. A more robust offshore wind system has opened up vast opportunities to maximize the use of marine energy. China's remarkable innovative achievements in offshore wind power, particularly the newly launched typhoon-resistant turbines, vividly demonstrate the formidable capabilities of its industrial system. "The country's wind power sector has maintained steady and orderly momentum throughout this year, highlighted by expanding installed capacity, a steadily rising share in total electricity generation, continuous technological breakthroughs and broadening international cooperation," said Pan Huimin, deputy director of the NEA's Department of New and Renewable Energy. With the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-30), the nation is establishing "expanding volume, enhancing quality and achieving reliable substitution" as its overarching theme. However, as the sector scales to unprecedented heights, Pan cautioned that it must navigate growing structural headwinds. "Wind power development is currently confronting mounting grid integration constraints, tightening factor supplies, declining project yields following full power marketization, and the insufficient realization of green environmental value," Pan said. To address these challenges, Pan emphasized the need to optimize regional development layouts, accelerate integrated energy models, adapt to competitive power markets and further strengthen international cooperation to benefit the broader global green transition. Industry leaders echoed the urgency of systemic upgrades, noting that grid integration is a shared global hurdle. Ben Backwell, CEO of the Global Wind Energy Council, pointed out that transmission infrastructure remains the most pressing bottleneck, as grid construction worldwide struggles to keep pace with surging renewable capacity. Backwell stressed that countries must invest more aggressively in grid technology, coordination and demand-side management. Furthermore, wind power enterprises can no longer act merely as hardware suppliers. They must provide comprehensive, integrated solutions. Pairing wind power with solar, energy storage and smart grid technologies will be essential to meet actual market demand and secure viable power tariffs in liberalized electricity markets, said Backwell. Reinforcing this perspective within the Chinese market, Liang Zhipeng, director of the renewable energy professional committee of the China Energy Research Society, stated that wind power has firmly become the backbone of China's energy security and green transition. He also advocated pioneering direct green power supply models to lower industrial end-user costs, driving collaborative innovation between artificial intelligence and electricity trading mechanisms, and establishing clear pathways to monetize the green premium of zero-carbon power.

title: Derivatives mkt seen as risk mgmt tool
body: Given escalated geopolitical tensions and mounting external uncertainties, experts suggest China's derivatives market should play a bigger role in meeting enterprises' growing demand for risk management amid sharp price volatility of commodities, while steadily advancing its opening-up to strengthen China's pricing power. Their comments were made on Thursday during the two-day 2026 Shanghai Derivatives Market Forum. Zhang Yue, deputy director of the department of futures supervision at the China Securities Regulatory Commission, said that opportunities outweigh challenges for China's derivatives market, as companies voiced urgent demand for risk management amid profound changes in the global economic and trade order. Against such a backdrop, efforts will be made to further enrich China's futures product supply to better meet industries' pricing autonomy and risk hedging demand. The trading mechanism should also be further optimized to lower costs for participating firms. More resources should be directed toward critical sectors so that the futures market can serve as a safe haven for industries, said Zhang. By leveraging China's large trading volume and outbound investment, the futures market should advance its institutional opening-up and more deeply participate in the formulation of international rules and standards. More derivatives should be opened up to overseas investors. Meanwhile, more overseas institutions should be introduced into the Chinese derivatives market to enhance the international influence of "China pricing", he added. Currently, overseas investors can directly participate in the trading of 11 derivatives listed in Shanghai, including the yuan-denominated crude oil futures launched in 2018 and bonded copper futures introduced in 2020. These are considered important references for global commodities pricing, Zhang said. As of end-September, 59 futures and options products were traded in Shanghai, 48 of which traded on the Shanghai Futures Exchange, with the remainder listed on the China Financial Futures Exchange. Apart from consolidating its strength in metal, energy and shipping futures, the SHFE will steadily advance the launch of natural gas and corrugated base paper derivatives, said the exchange's chairman Tian Xiangyang. Efforts will be made to launch strategic and fundamental products such as electricity futures. The application scenarios for "Shanghai prices" should be expanded, Tian said. One imminent example will be the London Metal Exchange steel hot-rolled coil Shanghai contract scheduled to trade at the LME on Oct 27. Since its launch in 2014, the SHFE HRC futures contract has grown into the world's largest flat steel futures contract. MiRan Park, LME's chief business officer, said the new arrangement will provide direct access to the global benchmark and grant offshore LME participants an easier entry point. He Qingwen, chairman of China Financial Futures Exchange, said that accelerated efforts are being made to develop index futures and options for ChiNext and the STAR Market to meet investors' needs of precisely managing the higher volatility of tech-heavy boards. Zhu Ning, professor at the Shanghai Advanced Institute of Finance at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, said that discerning, pricing and trading risks are the very basics of finance while the ultimate purpose of introducing derivatives is to help manage risks. Patient capital is usually more concerned about risks regarding macroeconomic growth, technological transformation, interest rates and foreign exchange, all of which can be effectively managed by derivatives. Therefore, substantial development of the derivatives market can provide diversified solutions, manage extreme risks via standardized or tailor-made contracts and help society to better understand long-term risks, Zhu said.

title: Apple Intelligence approved for China, Cook says in Shanghai
body: Apple Executive Chairman Tim Cook said in an interview on Thursday that Apple Intelligence has been approved for the Chinese market. Cook revealed that a test version will be released later this month. The first batch of features will include real-time translation, writing tools and image cleanup, while the AI-powered Siri will not be included in the initial rollout. The remarks came a day after China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology published updated telecom equipment network access license records showing that Apple's first foldable phone, the iPhone Duo (China model A3721), completed a license renewal on Sept 29. The updated documents added a filing number for the large language model installed on the device. A total of three large language models, including Apple Intelligence and Alibaba's Qwen, were newly filed this time, with filing numbers Shanghai-AppleZhiNeng-202506160057, Shanghai-TongYiWanXiang-202410090024 and ZheJiang-TongYiQianWen-20230901. The completion of the large language model filings is seen as a key step for Apple in advancing AI features in the Chinese market.

title: China's FDI equity stock ranks second globally: Commerce Ministry
body: BEIJING -- China's foreign direct investment equity stock reached 26.8 trillion yuan ($3.98 trillion) in 2025, ranking second globally and marking six consecutive years of growth, the Ministry of Commerce said Thursday, citing the latest annual reports from foreign-invested enterprises. A total of 461,000 foreign-invested enterprises filed annual reports last year, up 5.7 percent from 2024, according to data compiled by the ministry and other government departments. China's vast market offers foreign businesses opportunities to generate tangible returns, ministry representative He Yadong told a news conference, adding that China welcomes foreign companies seeking to expand their presence in the country and share in its development opportunities.
