The reporting companies posted an average profit margin of 8.7 percent in 2025. In the manufacturing sector, their profit margin was 2.2 percentage points higher than that of China's major industrial enterprises, the data showed. Foreign-invested enterprises accounted for one-third of China's total goods trade and one-seventh of the country's tax revenue in 2025. They also provided an average of more than 30 million jobs annually over the past five years, the ministry said. High-tech industries have become a bright spot for foreign investment in China. FDI in the sector rose 35.1 percent year-on-year to 200.26 billion yuan in the first eight months of this year, official data showed. China has stepped up efforts to stabilize foreign investment and direct more capital into advanced and high-value-added sectors. A 15-measure action plan unveiled in June this year aims to expand market access, streamline investment procedures, strengthen investment promotion and improve services for foreign investors. A new version of the Catalog of Encouraged Industries for Foreign Investment also took effect on Feb 1, encouraging foreign investment in advanced manufacturing, modern services, high-tech industries, energy conservation and environmental protection, as well as in China's central, western and northeastern regions.

title: Guangxi eyes stronger marine economy, deepens ASEAN ties
body: South China's Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region is accelerating the high-quality development of its marine economy and leveraging major infrastructure projects to deepen international trade cooperation, particularly with Southeast Asian nations, officials said. The region has witnessed robust growth in both its maritime sectors and overall foreign trade. During the first half of this year, Guangxi's marine gross product reached 137.7 billion yuan ($20.57 billion), marking a 6.8 percent year-on-year increase driven by advances in marine engineering equipment, offshore wind power and marine fisheries. This upward trajectory continued into the broader trade sector, with total foreign trade volume from January to August growing by 9.6 percent to 567.23 billion yuan. Lin Zenan, deputy director of Guangxi's Development and Reform Commission, noted that the region is actively optimizing its industrial layout along coastal areas, transportation corridors and inland waterways to build a modernized marine industrial system. Central to this economic transformation is the enhancement of maritime and inland connectivity. Beibu Gulf Port, a crucial international gateway, handled 312 million metric tons of cargo and 6.189 million twenty-foot equivalent units of containers in the first eight months of the year. Furthermore, the economic belt surrounding the newly operational Pinglu Canal generated a regional GDP of 712.63 billion yuan in the first half of the year, up 3.7 percent year-on-year. Lin emphasized that Guangxi is upgrading its infrastructure network, including railways and port facilities, to seamlessly integrate port operations with industrial and urban development, ultimately transforming port cities into highly livable and business-friendly hubs. Guangxi's strategic location has solidified its role as a vital hub for trade with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, which has maintained its position as Guangxi's largest trading partner for 26 consecutive years. From January to August, bilateral trade reached 284.69 billion yuan. Wang Xinhong, deputy director of the China (Guangxi) Pilot Free Trade Zone office, highlighted the region's success in creating a highly efficient supply chain for agricultural products. During the same period, Guangxi imported 30.45 billion yuan worth of fruits from ASEAN, accounting for more than one-third of the national total, with half of all durians imported into China passing through Guangxi ports. Additionally, the region is securing cross-border industrial supply chains, with intermediate goods trade surging by 18.5 percent to reach 410.09 billion yuan, ensuring stable manufacturing operations across the border. The China (Guangxi) Pilot Free Trade Zone has played a pivotal role in driving institutional openness and attracting global capital. During the 14th Five-Year Plan (2021-25) period, the region utilized $7.36 billion in actual foreign investment. Wang pointed out that the free trade zone is pioneering cross-border innovations, including the establishment of an artificial intelligence development path tailored for ASEAN applications, supported by AI cooperation agreements signed with eight ASEAN member states. The zone is also fostering a robust marine wind power industrial cluster. As the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 approaches implementation, local authorities are further streamlining cross-border data flows and expanding service trade in digital and cultural sectors. Meanwhile, local authorities are committed to balancing economic expansion with rigorous ecological security. Lin said Guangxi is implementing comprehensive environmental protection measures for coastal wetlands and mangroves, and has successfully promoted its marine ecological restoration experience nationwide. By prioritizing both technological innovation and green development, the region aims to ensure that its pursuit of a strong marine economy remains highly sustainable.

title: US companies to top CIIE exhibition area for eighth straight year
body: BEIJING -- US companies will top the exhibition area at the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) for the eighth time, with their area up 1,500 square meters from last year, an official said on Friday. The ninth CIIE will be held in Shanghai from Nov 5 to 10. Launched in 2018 as the world's first national-level expo dedicated to imports, the CIIE was designed to expand China's opening up and turn its vast market into a shared opportunity for the world. Preparations for the ninth CIIE are basically complete. A total of 162 countries, regions and international organizations will take part, with 4,142 overseas companies exhibiting, China's Vice-Minister of Commerce Yan Dong told a news conference. The overall exhibition area will exceed 440,000 square meters for the first time. In the enterprise exhibition, companies from the United States, Germany, Britain and France will lead the pack in terms of exhibition space. For the first time, the number of Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders attending the event will surpass 300. Additionally, over 2,000 companies will be exhibiting at the CIIE for the first time. This year's CIIE will feature over 200 representative global debuts and first-time exhibits. A variety of cutting-edge innovations that empower industries and enhance people's lives will be showcased together, including endoscopic surgical robots and cochlear implants. Ahead of this year's CIIE, matchmaking sessions themed under "export to China" were held in countries including Egypt, Germany and Britain, bringing procurement talks to the doorstep of trading partners. The CIIE is a prominent example of China's efforts to expand imports and provide more channels for quality products from around the world to enter the Chinese market. This commitment has remained high on China's agenda, and the results are tangible. According to the General Administration of Customs, China's imports reached 16.7 trillion yuan ($2.48 trillion) in the first nine months of this year, up 22.3 percent, the fastest growth since 2021. Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao said earlier this year that China's market holds huge potential, adding that the country will bring in more agricultural goods, quality consumer products, advanced technology equipment and key components. Meanwhile, platforms like the CIIE will be fully used to expand import channels, he said. "Exports and imports are like two wheels of a vehicle. The more balanced they are, the smoother and farther it goes," Wang said.

title: China-EU trade and investment consultation yields consensus, bringing stability to business cooperation: vice-minister
body: BEIJING - The second meeting of the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism has produced a series of consensus and outcomes that provide stability and certainty for business cooperation between Chinese and European companies, a Chinese commerce official has said. Ling Ji, vice-minister of commerce and deputy China international trade representative, made the remarks while meeting with Tobias Meyer, CEO of Germany-based logistics giant DHL Group, on Thursday. They exchanged views on DHL's development in China as well as China-Germany and China-EU economic and trade cooperation. Ling said the Chinese government remains firmly committed to high-standard opening up and is accelerating the building of a unified national market with an efficient, modern logistics network, which will provide broader development opportunities for Chinese and foreign logistics companies, including DHL. Meyer expressed confidence in the Chinese market, saying DHL is stepping up its investment in China and willing to contribute to the stable and healthy development of Germany-China and EU-China economic and trade relations. Chinese Minister of Commerce Wang Wentao and European Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maros Sefcovic jointly chaired the second meeting of the China-EU trade and investment consultation mechanism last week in Beijing. The two sides held pragmatic, productive discussions and agreed on a list of outcomes. The list set out 16 specific points of consensus covering trade and investment balance, export controls, intellectual property rights and World Trade Organization reform. Latest official data showed China's rising appeal to global businesses. The country's foreign direct investment (FDI) equity stock reached 26.8 trillion yuan ($3.99 trillion) in 2025, ranking second globally and marking six consecutive years of growth. High-tech industries have become a bright spot for foreign investment in China. FDI in the sector rose 35.1 percent year on year to 200.26 billion yuan in the first eight months of 2026.

title: Astribot brings T1 to North America, showcasing a physical AI stack built on 'Design for AI'
body: Astribot, a Shenzhen-based Physical AI company, brought its T1 humanoid robot to North America for the first time at IROS 2026, which took place from Sept 27 to Oct 1 at the David L. Lawrence Convention Center in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The company showcased its integrated approach to Physical AI spanning continuously improving AI models, an embodied operating system and a cable-driven robotic body. Rather than treating AI as a software layer added to an existing robot, Astribot follows a "Design for AI" philosophy, designing intelligence, the operating system and the physical body as an integrated system. Astribot places AI at the center of its Physical AI architecture. Its Lumo model family is designed to connect reasoning and action in physical environments, with the company developing models that can perceive, reason and execute tasks through real-world robots. Lumo-1 introduced Astribot's Reasoning-Action Foundation Model approach, while the company's subsequent Lumo-2 work explores latent world-action modeling for more complex physical tasks. The goal is not simply to produce a stronger model in isolation, but to continuously translate advances in AI into new capabilities for physical robots. Equipped with the Lumo-2 base model, T1 has demonstrated autonomous tidying of miscellaneous items into a backpack, combining decision-making with dexterous manipulation of deformable objects. Astribot is developing Lumo-2 to extend these capabilities to more complex household tasks; additional task capabilities depend on further training. Embodied OS: Connecting AI to the physical world An AI model alone does not make a robot useful. Astribot is therefore developing an embodied operating system designed to connect AI capabilities with people, robots and physical environments while lowering the barriers to interaction, development and use. For developers, T1 provides SDK and API access to capabilities including joint control, Cartesian motion and whole-body coordination, as well as access to sensor data. Astribot OS provides meta-packages and skill libraries that help developers orchestrate agentic behaviors and foundational functions. Its natural-language interface is designed to generate deployable robot applications from a single-line requirement. At the second Astribot OS Hackathon, which concluded on Sept 21 in Beijing, 15 teams developed and demonstrated more than 10 functional applications on T1 in 36 hours, according to the company. Robotic body: Designing the physical layer for AI The third layer is the robotic body itself. T1 is built around Astribot's cable-driven architecture, which is designed to support dexterous manipulation, compliant interaction and high-speed movement. The robot stands about 1.55 meters tall, weighs about 66 kilograms, has 23 degrees of freedom excluding end effectors, and supports up to 5 kilograms of payload per arm. T1 also backs automatic charging and quick battery replacement, while its modular design allows different end effectors, computing modules and sensors to be added for different tasks. Astribot's "Design for AI" approach reflects the company's view that the physical body should be designed around what AI needs to perceive and do, rather than optimized independently from intelligence. In a cable-driven system, the company aims to combine dexterity, compliance and backdrivability with the ability to expose richer physical interaction information to the intelligence stack. This makes the body more than an actuator platform: it becomes part of the system through which AI interacts with the physical world. The three layers form a continuous development loop: AI generates capabilities, the embodied OS connects those capabilities to the robot and its users, and the physical body executes them in the real world. T1 does not learn autonomously in real time during deployment. Instead, Astribot collects multimodal data from robot operation and teleoperation, processes and curates that data, retrains models such as Lumo-2, and deploys updated skills through over-the-air updates or on-site installation and calibration. Customers can choose to collect data for dedicated model training or during autonomous task execution. For Astribot, this is the foundation of its approach to Physical AI: AI that grows by doing. T1 is designed as a developer-accessible Physical AI platform for researchers, developers and real-world applications. With US pricing starting at $18,000, T1 combines modular hardware, developer interfaces, VR-based teleoperation and AI capabilities. US customers can order T1 now, with immediate delivery available. Astribot is a Shenzhen-based Physical AI company developing AI models, an embodied operating system and robotic bodies as an integrated system under its "Design for AI" philosophy. Its T1 platform brings together cable-driven robotics and developer-accessible tools for physical AI research and applications. Learn more at https://www.astribot.com/. Email: lin@astribot.com

title: Roger Federer said shareholder-athlete model gives On edge as it expands beyond running
body: Roger Federer believes sportswear brand On Holding's strategy of making elite athletes long-term business partners rather than traditional endorsers is helping fuel its expansion into new sports, as the Swiss company looks to replicate its success in running across tennis, football and golf. Speaking during his first visit to Shenzhen, the 20-time Grand Slam champion said becoming a co-entrepreneur at On fundamentally changed his relationship with the company, allowing him to contribute to product development and long-term strategy instead of simply promoting products. "The way I was approached by the founders was to be part of them—not just be a testimonial or a brand ambassador, but to be a partner," Federer said in an interview. "You have a different mindset. You think much more long term." Federer's comments offer a glimpse into a business model that has become central to On's growth strategy as the Swiss sportswear company expands beyond its running roots. Unlike conventional endorsement deals that typically last only a few years, equity partnerships encourage athletes to help shape product development, brand strategy and new business opportunities, aligning their interests with the company's long-term growth. "I think having a key partner in the company definitely changes the outlook," Federer said. "It could potentially change how brands and athletes work together." Federer has become one of the best-known examples of the model since joining On as an investor and partner in 2019. Since retiring from professional tennis, he has spent more time working with the company's product teams at its Zurich headquarters, helping design footwear while contributing to broader brand development. Among his latest projects is The ROGER Pro series of tennis shoes, which combines technologies developed for On's running shoes with the demands of professional tennis. "I see that as a way to give back—to create a really good tennis shoe for players to stay injury-free, enjoy themselves on court, chase their biggest dreams and win the titles they want to win," Federer said. He said On's relatively short history in tennis has become an advantage because the company is willing to challenge conventional thinking about tennis footwear rather than follow established industry norms. The athlete-partnership model is now being extended into other sports. Last month, On unveiled plans to expand into football and golf as part of its strategy to become a broader premium sportswear brand. The company has signed French football star Kylian Mbappe as a partner while appointing former Arsenal and France striker Thierry Henry as director of football. Federer said he sees parallels between Mbappe's role in football and his own experience helping build On's tennis business. "I may have been something of a blueprint within the company for how On entered tennis," he said. "Now Kylian is coming into football." He added that consumers will be able to watch football products evolve through direct collaboration between athletes and designers, including products using On's LightSpray manufacturing technology. During his Shenzhen visit, Federer took part in an On-hosted event, including playing with local young players and watching a drone show titled "Thanks for Playing." The campaign, which has been brought to China for three consecutive years, supports grassroots tennis development. The push to deepen its engagement with Chinese consumers comes as Asia-Pacific becomes an increasingly important growth region for On. The region contributed more than 20 percent of global revenue in the second quarter, with strong momentum across Japan, South Korea and China. "It's important to persevere, keep dreaming and stay positive," Federer said. "The company is in an amazing place with great momentum, and I hope we can keep the growth going."

title: Huiyang's guitar industry hits high notes
body: The first thing you notice is what's missing: No solid wood. No spruce top, either, and no rosewood back. In a workshop in Huiyang, a district of Huizhou, Guangdong province, a guitar is being tested that looks like the instrument you know but doesn't behave like one at all. The guitar is made of carbon fiber. And somewhere inside, a chip is quietly doing the work of an entire band. This is what Hu Haiming, founder of the Chinese smart instrument brand Enya Music, has spent the past decade arguing for. "The quality of a guitar primarily depends on its sound quality, user experience and its adaptability to different scenarios, not just the type of wood used," he said. That conviction has been the company's compass since 2011, when it set up shop in Huiyang and began pouring resources into new materials and smart hardware later. Hu is blunt about why. "Sticking to traditional solid wood manufacturing will never allow us to catch up with high-end overseas brands — the only path forward is through innovation in new materials and technologies to create proprietary core products," he said. The ground he's standing on has a longer history than the technology might suggest. Huiyang's guitar industry began in the early 1990s, when businesspeople from China's Taiwan island opened factories in the district. For years, those factories made guitars for other brands. The profit margins tell the story: Single-product margins hovered around 5 percent. "The lack of an independent brand and pricing power, coupled with the limitations in the production capacity of solid wood materials and unstable yield rates, severely restricted the industry's development," Hu said. His answer was to build outward. Drawing on the supply chain advantages of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area, the company set up three research centers — in Guangzhou and Shenzhen in Guangdong, and in the United States — devoted to composite materials and intelligent interaction technology. Three years of work produced the Enya NEXG in 2021, the world's first carbon-fiber smart guitar. Then, in 2024, came the Cyber, capable of simulating the sounds of more than 20 instruments. "Coupled with an intelligent interactive system, the Cyber guitar significantly lowered the barrier to entry for music, helping realize the concept of one guitar as an entire band," Hu said. The market responded. During Amazon Prime Day in June, the company hit the top of the online giant's global sales charts in three categories at once — electric guitars, acoustic-electric guitars and ukuleles. Its achievements reflect a bigger picture: Guitar companies in Huiyang have done well in the international market, as the nation's manufacturing industry continues to upgrade. After more than 30 years, the district has built a complete guitar supply chain. Within a two-kilometer radius of Qiuchang subdistrict, raw materials, components and production equipment can all be sourced in one stop. But the reliance on original equipment manufacturing, or OEM, with thin margins and a long grind at the low end, had become impossible to ignore. As a result, Huizhou Quanfeng Recreation Products suspended all of its OEM business in 2020 and threw its weight behind its own brand, Farida. Years of manufacturing experience and the support of foreign technical consultants gave Farida a fast foothold. "We are now making full efforts to enter the high-end market," said Cai Laifeng, the company's chairman.

title: Pulitzer Prize-winner documents BRI's impact
body: At 72, most people might be thinking about slowing down. But Liu Heung Shing had other plans. The Pulitzer Prize-winning Chinese American photographer wrapped up a three-year, 270,000-kilometer journey across four continents at the end of last year, and has turned the feat into a book documenting the Belt and Road Initiative. "I think the BRI could very well be one of the greatest projects of the 21st century," Liu said during his book sharing session in Shanghai on Sept 12. "What intrigued me most was how China would make it work across different cultures, religions and levels of economic development," he added. Official figures show that since 2013, more than 150 countries and 30 international organizations have signed BRI cooperation documents. In 2025, China's overseas engagement under the BRI reached about $213.5 billion, according to a study by Fudan University and Australia's Griffith University. That included $128.4 billion in construction contracts and $85.2 billion in investments. Liu began documenting China in 1976. Over the decades, his work has taken him across China, the former Soviet Union and beyond. For more than a decade, he has been mainly based in Shanghai, where he founded the Shanghai Center of Photography. In 2023, he turned his lens to the BRI, ultimately traveling through 21 countries and 50 regions. "You have to be there. You have to use your ears, your eyes, and observe people's body language," Liu said. "Otherwise, the story lacks global perspective and breadth." The journey is documented in Old Road, New Connections: China Builds a Different World, a 508-page photo book featuring more than 330 photographs. The project was jointly launched with ShanghaiTech University, where Liu is a distinguished professor. Peter Hessler, author of River Town: Two Years on the Yangtze, wrote on the book's cover that the images — "Chinese cars being sold in Tehran, a Chinese-built train delivering pilgrims to attend the Hajj in Mecca" — make it "almost impossible to grasp the scale of change". Beyond that, what emerges from the book is not simply a portrait of infrastructure, but of people — those building it, living alongside it and creating connections across cultures. For some, that means working on railways, ports, water treatment plants and mines. In Kazakhstan, Liu visited a water treatment plant that Chinese engineers were handing over to the local government — a facility serving 170,000 people. In Indonesia, he spent months negotiating access to the cockpit of the Jakarta-Bandung high-speed railway, where Chinese drivers were training Indonesian operators. In the Democratic Republic of Congo, he descended 1,546 meters underground to photograph Chinese engineers working alongside local miners. But the BRI also takes shape in everyday life. In Kashgar, in Northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region, Liu met a man from the Uygur ethnic group, who had studied at Fuzhou University and now runs a cafe with his Tanzanian wife. Others are building bridges of another kind — across languages and cultures. In Kenya, Liu met a 32-year-old Chinese graduate who had spent a decade working in Africa and had no plans to return to China for work. He also met a student in Uzbekistan who hoped to study in China and return home to work as a translator. Liu said he did not set out with a predetermined conclusion. "I don't know what I'm going to see until I get there," he said. He followed what he encountered on the road, seeing the book simply as a record — not an argument. "You do the best you can, put it on the table, and let people look at it and form their own understanding," he said. For Camille Whitworth, an American teacher who has lived in China for 13 years, Liu's book offers a perspective on China and the BRI that many Americans rarely encounter. "It's helping people out, making connections, having business connections and family connections with China," she said. "Chinese people are everywhere and an important part of the world community. This book is a great way to document China's relationship with the rest of the world." Liu's journey was not without risks. Before leaving for the Democratic Republic of Congo, he asked his lawyer to prepare a will. He also needed five vaccinations over eight weeks. He left Iran before Israeli strikes hit the country, and he left the DRC before local conflicts escalated. "I don't know if I was chasing them, or they were chasing me," Liu joked. After three years on the road, now 75, Liu said he was ready for a break. "I hope you can be kind to me," he said. "I really need a rest." "There are still one or two ideas warming up."

title: Ancient Silk Road hub comes alive in Beijing exhibition
body: The Qiuci state, located in what is now Kuqa in Aksu prefecture, Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region, was a thriving, strategically important hub on the ancient Silk Road, where different civilizations and cultures met, exchanged ideas, and blended. Jiangu Wansui Renmin Xi  (May the firm and enduring last forever, and may the people rejoice), an ongoing exhibition at the Chinese Traditional Culture Museum in Beijing, showcases the distinctive and profound cultural heritage that flourished at the height of Qiuci and has been preserved for millennia. Reproductions and digital recreations bring back the splendor of Qiuci's cave art, which traces the spread of Buddhism in China. Its music and dance, once absorbed into classical Chinese performing arts, have been revived by modern artists. Re-created household courtyards, furnished with everyday items such as pottery, carpets, and hats, offer an immersive experience. For those who have never been to Kuqa, or who are planning a visit, the exhibition, which runs until April 5, offers a vivid and comprehensive introduction to the region.

title: Sitar virtuoso Anoushka Shankar makes China debut
body: Sitar virtuoso Anoushka Shankar has made her China debut, with Beijing serving as the opening stop of her Chinese tour on Oct 14, bringing her distinctive blend of Indian classical music, contemporary rhythms and musical experimentation to Chinese audiences. The 13-time Grammy nominee is the daughter of legendary Indian sitar master Ravi Shankar, whose contributions helped introduce Indian classical music to audiences around the world. Following in her father's footsteps while forging her own artistic path, Anoushka has developed a musical language that bridges tradition and innovation. Her work moves fluidly between the intricate structures of Indian classical music, contemporary rhythmic patterns, minimalist influences and improvisation. Drawing on a wide range of musical traditions, she continues to explore new possibilities for the sitar while remaining deeply connected to her cultural heritage. Her show in Beijing was part of the ongoing 29th Beijing Music Festival. The program for her China tour — Shanghai on Oct 16 and Guangzhou on Oct 18 — features a selection of original and collaborative works, alongside  Fire Night , a composition by her father. It also includes a piece written with her sister, offering audiences a glimpse into the family's shared musical legacy. Her performances offer Chinese audiences an opportunity to experience the versatility of the sitar in a contemporary setting, where classical traditions meet experimentation and diverse musical influences.

title: Treasures reveal the power of a Shang queen
body: The extraordinary status Fu Hao, a royal woman of the late Shang Dynasty (c. 16th-11th century BC), enjoyed is reflected in the wealth of objects buried with her. They include bronzes inlaid with gold and turquoise, seashell coins and red agate stones, offering a glimpse into the riches of her time. These artifacts are on display at the Yinxu Museum in Anyang, Henan province, where Fu Hao's tomb was discovered in 1976. Their rarity and beauty fascinate visitors from China and abroad, while scholars see them as valuable sources of historical insight. Zhang Changping, a history professor at Wuhan University in Hubei province, says the objects point to trade between the Shang Dynasty and other cultures, including those beyond China. They also testify to the power of Wu Ding, Fu Hao's husband and the Shang ruler of the time. Zhang shared his findings at a recent forum in Anyang, held to mark the 50th anniversary of the tomb's discovery. The city is home to the Yinxu Ruins, the archaeological site of the late Shang capital. The forum brought together scholars to discuss their latest research on Shang history and explore ways to bring their findings to the public. Beyond the stories of Fu Hao and Wu Ding, they sought to illuminate the wider world in which the royal couple lived.

title: Silla exhibition dazzles in gold and the spirit of the East
body: From dazzling gold crowns, vibrant glassware and jade artifacts to majestic Buddhist sculptures, the ongoing exhibition Beneath the Golden Crown: Highlights of Silla's Treasures at Shanghai Museum East presents one of China's first showcases devoted to the ancient civilization of Silla on the Korean Peninsula. The exhibition has been organized by the Shanghai Museum in collaboration with the Gyeongju National Museum in South Korea. Running from Sept 23 to Jan 18, 2027, it brings together 260 objects that distill the spirit of Silla culture, placing them alongside works from the Shanghai Museum's collection to explore the exercise of power and the cultural landscape, to read the lives and aesthetic pursuits of the Silla people, and to retrace the kingdom's rise and decline. Silla was one of the most important ancient polities on the Korean Peninsula. According to the later chronicle Samguk Sagi, its history is believed to date to around 57 BC, with its rule ending in 935. The Gyeongju National Museum is dedicated to preserving, displaying, and researching Silla history and culture, second in scale only to the National Museum of Korea (Seoul), according to Yoon Sangdeok, its director. "We hope this exhibition allows visitors to experience the depth and sublime beauty of Silla culture from a fresh perspective and enjoy a meaningful journey connecting the past and the present," Yoon says. "We also hope to continue exchange and cooperation between the Gyeongju National Museum and the Shanghai Museum through this exhibition." The Silla exhibition is a response to the Shanghai Museum's 2021 exhibition of ancient Chinese bronze culture at the National Museum of Korea and represents the fruits of that bilateral cooperation, Yoon told the media at the exhibition opening in Shanghai on Sept 23. The exhibition features several important artifacts designated as South Korean national treasures that are rarely shown abroad. "We went through a long, complicated process to gain official approval, because it was important to show them at this exhibition in Shanghai," he says. It offers a multifaceted perspective on Silla through three themes: The Culture of Gold, International Exchanges and Buddhist Art. Magnificent metalwork, represented by the gold crowns, marks the most prominent chapter of Silla culture. The Silla people gained a deep understanding of gold as a material and used it to express supreme power. The Gyeongju museum's director explains that crowns made of high-purity gold have only been excavated from burial sites in Gyeongju, the Silla capital. An exquisite crown unearthed in 1921 is among the gold artifacts at the exhibition's center. Its details imitate tree branches and deer antlers, reflecting the ancient Silla people's worship of nature: the tree, with its roots reaching deep into the earth and its branches extending high into the sky, was viewed as a medium connecting heaven and earth, while the deer was revered as a mythical creature. According to Zhao Jia, a curator in the Shanghai Museum's exhibition department, the museum selected objects from its own collection to highlight the cultural exchanges between China's Tang Dynasty (618-907) and Silla. "The polychrome-glazed pottery figurines reflect how Tang Dynasty clothing styles influenced Silla, from officials' robes to women's attire," she says. The Green-glazed Biyong-shaped Pottery Inkstone from the Shanghai Museum is displayed alongside the Clay Six-footed Inkstone from Gyeongju, highlighting their similar design details. "China and the Korean Peninsula share deeply rooted ties, as we are geographically contiguous and culturally connected," says Chu Xiaobo, director of the Shanghai Museum. "Gyeongju, as the capital of Silla, with its majestic royal tombs and numerous Buddhist temples, serves as an 'open-air museum' that preserves Silla's historical character. Through this joint endeavor, we hope to employ these cultural treasures as a bridge across mountains and seas. May this exhibition renew our bond of mutual learning and exchange, and jointly showcase the open and inclusive spirit of the East."

title: Late comic artist preserves essence of childhood
body: Digital gadgets have become "besties" for today's youth. In the old days, younger generations had to use their creativity to invent games to play — making faces to make each other laugh, using low benches as hurdles in race competitions, and taking turns bending down while others jumped over them. Playgrounds were shared courtyards or long alleyways. These warm, pleasant moments once enriched the childhood of He Youzhi (1922-2016), the late comic artist renowned for leaving a body of picture books and illustrations tugged at the heartstrings of several generations of Chinese people. His dozens of works depict the simple children's games he once enjoyed while growing up in Shanghai's Nongtang alleyway communities. Some are now on show at He Youzhi's Art Besides Lianhuanhua , an exhibition running at the Art Museum of the Beijing Fine Art Academy until Oct 15. He's paintings, with their minimalist style, document details of people's social lives decades ago, many of which customs, such as children's games, have now all but disappeared.

title: Practice makes a perfect day out
body: Enjoying a day at the Rolex Shanghai Masters does not always require a premier seat at the center court for a heavyweight "main event". The Qizhong Tennis Center is offering a carnival of activities — live music performed on shaded lawns and meet-and-greets with star players and celebrities — for just 60 yuan ($9) a ticket for a ground pass. The first stop for many, though, is the Royal Caribbean Masters Practice Court. A 1,200-seat open training facility purposely built last year to provide fans a better viewing experience, it has proved a hit, with spectators lining up at the entrance, even before the first match of the day swings off, just to get a front-row peek at their favorite stars' practice drills. Despite an early exit this year in Shanghai, 24-time major winner Novak Djokovic easily drew the largest crowd to his training session at the court, where the four-time tournament champion fine-tuned his strokes, tested serve placement and improvised on shots during extended rallies just meters away from his "NoleFam" supporters. The Serbian great acknowledged fans and bantered with them by mimicking his hitting partner whenever he took a break, after eliciting "oohs" and "aahs" from them with either a delicate drop shot or a crisp backhand winner during the rallies. Young Spanish phenom Carlos Alcaraz appeared an equally popular crowd-pleaser at the practice court, with spectators leaning forward, phones and autograph pens at the ready, breaking into applause whenever the seven-time Grand Slam champion waved to the stands after hitting a couple of shots at full intensity. Watching from up close, fans get a real sense for how hard the pros club their shots, how seriously they approach their, sometimes tedious, warm-up routines and how fun their improvised drills can be. Greek former world No 3 Stefanos Tsitsipas turned his first open practice on Sunday into a fun challenge, as the tournament's 2019 semifinalist hit against some lucky, randomly selected fans using a pan as his makeshift racket. Alcaraz stepped it up the next day by pulling off the famed "Impossible Shot" challenge at the practice court with jaw-dropping accuracy. The task seems fiendishly simple on paper: strike a forehand cleanly through a tiny target hole, cut barely wider than a tennis ball on a vertical board, from behind the baseline. The Spanish maestro made it look even easier by threading a forehand straight through with his first attempt — before some fans had even raised their phone cameras — drawing a roar from the stands. Wu Xingrun was among the fist-clenching fans watching the Spaniard conjure his magic from courtside, and confessed it was an even better show than spending over 10 times the money to watch a match. "I think the opportunity to watch and observe the star players from close range, and even exchange a few words with them, is what a true tennis fan would appreciate," said Wu, an amateur player himself who works in finance. "To have this bigger training facility with seating prepared for us is a bonus." Tournament director Michael Luevano said it was the Chinese fans' growing passion for the sport that pushed organizers to upgrade the facilities, keeping pace with other prestigious events. "We've seen the success other Masters have had (with practice court access) and we wanted to take it to the next level," Luevano stated on the tournament's official website. "Chinese fans love to be close to the players. We do activations with the players and the crowd is always enthusiastic and interactive." Once a young boy who was just as interested then as his fans are now in following the pros' training sessions, Canada's current world No 5 Felix Auger-Aliassime learned how to get creative to watch his heroes practice at his home Masters 1000 tournament in Montreal back in the day. "I'd get up on my tiptoes and try to see between the holes in the fences," recalled the Montreal native, who was forced to retire from his fourth-round match against Casper Ruud on Wednesday due to an apparent knee injury. "I always found it more intriguing to go to the practices, to see the players from up close, how they grip the racket and their intensity," he also told the tournament's website. After a few practice sessions at Qizhong, the 26-year-old, who reached the quarterfinals last year in Shanghai, said he wished he'd had this kind of access when he was young. "It's a great setup for the fans. It has great visibility from all around the court, which is not always the case. Fans can sit and enjoy it like it's a real match. "I can relate to the fans, because I was that kid once."

title: From bouldering to BMX, emerging sports gain a grip
body: As the National Day holiday drew to a close, young people took turns tackling a rock climbing wall at a gym in Xi'an, Shaanxi province. Some carefully tested each hold before moving upward, while others dropped back onto the mats and prepared to try again. For Zhao Yu'an, a young climber at the gym, the appeal lay in the challenge itself — figuring out how to complete a route and sharing the experience with friends. Earlier in the holiday, thousands of kilometers away, Chinese climbers had faced a very different test at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games. Zhang Yuetong won the women's bouldering gold medal, while Chu Shouhong claimed the men's speed climbing title with a time of 4.71 seconds. From street culture, climbing communities and grassroots training spaces to the Asian Games and Olympics, emerging sports such as skateboarding, sport climbing and breaking are reaching wider audiences in China. Major competitions have brought these disciplines greater visibility and helped establish clearer pathways for elite athletes. Their performances, in turn, inspire more young people to take up the sports.

title: NBA holds court in Macao
body: With Kyrie Irving's long-anticipated return and Kevin Durant's star power setting Macao abuzz, the 2026 NBA China Games have once again consolidated the league's robust presence in its biggest international market. By bringing in two franchises that both enjoy strong ties with the country, the 2026 NBA China Games tour, held in the special administrative region for a second straight year, has provided even greater fanfare than last year's showpiece, after the Houston Rockets and Dallas Mavericks split two games on the league's 15th preseason trip to China. Drawn by his first game in 19 months, after a lengthy recovery from a knee injury, Irving's vocal supporters, draped in Dallas blue and wearing cowboy hats, lit up the packed Venetian Arena from the tipoff on Sunday night, as Irving scored a layup in the opening possession to set the tone for a team-high 17 points in the Mavericks' 132-115 win over the Rockets. Irving's strong comeback made up for the no-show of his All-Star counterpart Durant, who skipped the second game after having led the Rockets as they blasted the Mavericks 135-117 by scoring 15 points on the opening night of the two-game series on Friday. The two exhibitions capped off a five-day hoops festival that took the city by storm, as a glittering cast of NBA stars that also included Dallas'2025-26 Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg, Houston's Turkish center Alperen Sengun and veteran guard Fred VanVleet drew massive fan turnouts wherever they appeared. Lengthy queues of fans donning their favorite players' jerseys snaked past the entrance of NBA House — a free, interactive fan carnival staged at The Venetian Macao — before each game, eager to catch a glimpse of their idols during meets-and-greets with visiting NBA legends, such as Ray Allen, the league's all-time third-highest-ranked 3-point shooter, Chris Bosh, an 11-time league All-Star and Jeremy Lin, an Asian fan favorite. Outside the arena, fans also trailed the players across the city to each of their endorsement events, team photo calls and media interviews, gathering at their hotel lobby for autographs and photos day and night. They knew it would be crazy before arriving, but the energy surrounding their games in Macao still managed to blow the minds of even the most sought-after stars. "Huge thank you to all my China fans who showed up outside of the hotel, giving me a lot of love, always feeling unconditional support," Irving said during the post-game news conference on Sunday. After Thursday's practice, reflecting on his long-held ties with China through the fans and partnerships with local sponsors, Irving said: "You just always want to make sure that you perform well for the people who love you ... I love to humanize my connection with my supporters, always making them feel they were acknowledged. "I've been coming here since I was 19, so this is an honor that I carry with me, just being aware of the support that I've enjoyed from here and having developed a lot of relationships over here. "Coming back here feels like a second home now." The Rockets, however, had expected more of a "home team" reception coming in, with the franchise's 2002 top draft pick Yao Ming, a basketball Hall of Famer hailing from Shanghai, cheering them on courtside. Having retired in 2011, Yao's towering influence in helping promote NBA basketball in China, while enhancing sports exchanges between China and the United States, has been hailed by the younger Rockets. "I think we all know how big the Rockets are in China," said Houston's veteran guard VanVleet, who also made a strong comeback from a torn right ACL by scoring 17 points to go with seven assists in his team's opening win on Friday. "Yao was a legend and just a great ambassador for us. And, obviously, the fans are very passionate and crazy about Kevin (Durant) as well, so that definitely helps (us) earn great support. It's been an incredible trip and we're having a lot of fun." The Mavericks have also played a pioneering role in introducing Chinese talent to the NBA by selecting former Team China center Wang Zhizhi with the 36th overall pick in the 1999 draft. Two years later, Wang was allowed to join the club and became the first-ever Chinese player to compete in the NBA on April 5, 2001.

title: PSG brings embattled City back down to earth
body: MANCHESTER, England — Manchester City wowed fans with a spectacular fireworks show and a highlights reel of some of its greatest hits before Wednesday's home Champions League clash with Paris Saint-Germain. It quickly went downhill from there. In what could be interpreted as a latest display of defiance from the embattled club — which has been found guilty of widespread financial wrongdoing — City produced a slick pre-match show reminding supporters of the good times with footage of its most iconic moments on the Etihad Stadium's big screens. On the field, however, the highlights belonged to PSG in a blistering first-half performance, which saw the back-to-back European champion race to a 3-0 lead at the break, including two goals in quick succession. And even if City mounted a spirited second-half fightback, a 4-2 loss brought the club down to earth after the triumphalism that some found off-putting in the wake of Sunday's 3-0 Premier League victory against Liverpool. "Against this kind of team it's already difficult when you are 0-0, and then, in two minutes, you concede two goals, probably we lost a little bit of balance," City coach Enzo Maresca said. "I think we can learn many things. First of all, even if we concede two goals against probably the best team in Europe at the moment, we need to continue to do the right things." With former City manager Pep Guardiola watching on from the stands, PSG's first-half blitz sobered the atmosphere after the rousing pre-match show. Desire Doue, Ousmane Dembele and Vitinha all scored, and the defending champion created numerous other chances to extend its lead. This was City's first home game since an independent panel found that it broke Premier League rules by artificially inflating its revenue by more than $1 billion over nearly a decade on its way to dominating English football. City has appealed, leaving an air of uncertainty over the club's future and the season as a whole, with potential punishments including a huge fine, points deductions or even expulsion from England's top flight. The Emirati-owned club has always pleaded its innocence, and, along with its fans, has been resolute in its determination to clear its name. This was the first chance to put on a show of solidarity at its home stadium since the verdict. A huge banner was hung with the words: "I know I am, I'm sure I am, I'm City 'til I die". The highlight reel included Sergio Aguero's famous title-winning goal in 2012, as well as other moments predating the Abu Dhabi takeover in 2008. In the stands, Guardiola — on his first return to the club since stepping down at the end of last season — sat behind club chief executive Ferran Soriano. Despite the verdict, City has refused to be bowed and the win against Liverpool was evidence its players could put the outside noise to one side and focus on the field. PSG, however, was a different story. Another club that has benefited wildly from investment from the Middle East through its Qatari backers, the French giant has built the finest team in Europe and lived up to that billing by sweeping City aside in the first half. It was the type of performance to suggest it is capable of a Champions League three-peat, emulating the all-time king of Europe Real Madrid. At the break, it felt like City could be on the end of a humbling defeat. However, Maresca's team managed to turn a would-be rout into a thrilling clash. Erling Haaland scored two goals, two efforts came back off the woodwork and another chance was cleared off the line. Maghnes Akliouche's goal, in between Haaland's double, effectively ensured there would be no comeback, before Ferran Torres failed to score a fifth for the visitor from the penalty spot. "It's not important to be the best in the competition now, it's important to be the best in the final," PSG coach Luis Enrique said.

title: Top seed Sabalenka falls at first hurdle in Wuhan
body: WUHAN — A frustrated Aryna Sabalenka suffered a second successive early tournament exit, as her bid for a fourth Wuhan Open title was foiled by American world No 31 Ann Li 3-6, 6-4, 7-6 (5) in round two, while China's Guo Hanyu advanced to the round of 16 on Wednesday. The top-seeded Sabalenka fell to Nikola Bartunkova in the third round at the China Open last week and squandered a 6-3, 4-2 lead against Li to stumble at her very first hurdle in Wuhan. The Belarusian four-time major winner lost her No 1 ranking to Elena Rybakina last month and has not won a title since March. Playing with protective taping around her right knee, Sabalenka was in control of the match until Li swung the momentum in her direction halfway through the second set. Sabalenka asked for the trainer when she was broken early in the decider and appeared to be struggling with her movement. Still, she was able to wipe a 2-5 deficit, saving nine match points along the way. Li steadied the ship, though, and finished the job in two hours and 27 minutes on her 10th opportunity, setting up a last-16 clash with Indonesia's Janice Tjen. "I think on some of those match points, I was about to lose my mind. I was about to crash out. In the end, you just have to realize, I didn't play badly and she just played really well," Li said. "And, so, you have to just play point by point. I knew that, if I stayed there, I could get to the situation again. "For me, it just shows that I'm trying to improve every day from every match. My only goal was to improve from the last match I played," Li added. "I know that if I play my tennis and I stay positive, and I stay physical and intense, I can win any match." China's Guo outlasted Katie Volynets of the United States 6-4, 4-6, 7-6(3) to reach the last 16 at a WTA 1000 event for the first time. "It was another very tough match today, and the score stayed close," Guo said. "Until the last point, there was no way to say the match was over, so I just tried to give everything I had from start to finish and do the best I could. I'm happy to have won another match." Guo next plays fifth-seeded Elina Svitolina of Ukraine. "It will be an even harder match, and I will prepare more tonight," Guo said. "The first thing is to recover well, so that I can step on court tomorrow at 100 percent." Meanwhile, second-seeded Jessica Pegula, the runner-up in Wuhan last year, was also sent packing. The American suffered a 2-6, 7-6(7), 6-3 upset at the hands of Jelena Ostapenko, wasting three match points along the way. Ostapenko is the first player to beat Pegula in her opening match at a WTA 1000 event since Indian Wells two and a half years ago, snapping Pegula's 22-event winning streak in openers at this level. Earlier, six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek launched her Wuhan Open campaign by triumphing 6-2, 6-1 in an all-Polish battle against lucky loser Magdalena Frech. Swiatek posted her 40th victory of the season in one hour and 42 minutes and no longer has Sabalenka as a potential roadblock in the quarterfinals. "We know each other pretty well, so I just wanted to focus on being consistent and playing as well as possible," Swiatek, the seventh seed, said of Frech. "I know she is always running to every ball and sometimes using the power of the opponent, so I wanted to not play too crazy but play solid and I'm happy that I did that," said Swiatek, who is chasing a qualification spot for the year-end WTA Finals. Wimbledon finalist Karolina Muchova weathered a three-hour storm to come through 3-6, 7-6 (1), 7-6(4) against American qualifier Caty McNally to extend her record in tiebreaks this season to a perfect 10-0.

title: Martinez blasts United bosses after latest loss
body: Lisandro Martinez added to Manchester United's troubled start to the season by calling out the club's hierarchy following a 2-0 loss to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League on Tuesday. In a post-game interview, Martinez questioned the club's offseason recruitment after it had secured a return to the Champions League this season. "I have to control myself a lot, but sometimes it's a reflection in the mirror of how our club is at the moment," Martinez told Amazon Prime. "We had a fantastic season last season. And, now, we expect more from the top ... to bring in more players to compete, because many teams brought in many players, (like) Atletico today, they have an amazing team and they deserved to win. "I expect more from our technical director. I have to be honest, as the players, we have to do more, but it's just as important to build a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night." Jason Wilcox is United's director of football and the club spent around $213 million on players like Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in the summer, but it has endured a difficult start to the campaign. Defeat in Madrid extended United's winless run to five games in all competitions. It has won only once in the Premier League and is 13th in the standings. "Last season, we did everything, we created the base to be an amazing team," Martinez said. "It's annoying — disappointing — to come here and I'm not seeing my team trying to get an amazing result here." Pablo Barrios scored in the first minute for Atletico and Ademola Lookman sealed victory in the 79th, scoring five minutes after United was reduced to 10 men when a foul by Leny Yoro was upgraded to a red card following a VAR review. The latest setback will add to the pressure on United coach Michael Carrick. "You start changing, changing, changing manager. But what about other areas?" Martinez said. "I can't say more." 'This victory is for Koke' Man United has made its worst domestic start in 40 years and this league-phase defeat in the Spanish capital was another blow. Carrick handed Baleba his first start for the club since arriving from Brighton in the summer, as well as pushing captain Bruno Fernandes out to the right side. Atletico was without its skipper Koke, after the death of his mother, while coach Diego Simeone started Julian Alvarez for the first time this season at the Metropolitano Stadium, after he tried to force a departure this summer. "As well as for the team, it was very important (to win) for Koke and all of his family," said Barrios. "It's a very tough day for them. This victory is for them. "Getting the goal so soon helped us manage the game later. I'm really happy for the win." Atletico's "ultras" ordered the team and its supporters to "defend what we love" with a banner display before kickoff, and the Rojiblancos were ahead after just 50 seconds. Alex Baena found a way in behind United's defense and cut the ball across for Barrios, with United center-back Ayden Heaven unable to keep the midfielder's shot from crossing the line. Barrios held up six fingers to pay tribute to Koke. "It was really tough news for everyone and I said that, if I scored, I would do that," added Barrios. Carrick had said it was important to get off to a fast start, but his team was unable to follow his instructions. Bryan Mbeumo might have equalized for the visitor, nudging the ball through Cristian Romero's legs, but firing just wide. Alejandro Grimaldo came inches away from extending Atletico's lead with a free kick, which hit the corner between the post and the crossbar. The host thought it had a second when Johnny Cardoso finished neatly from the edge of the box before halftime, but the goal was disallowed after a VAR review showed the ball had struck Marcos Llorente's hand during the buildup. Carrick withdrew playmaker Fernandes, looking ahead to the weekend trip away to bitter rival Leeds in the English top flight, where an improvement in performance is badly needed. "It is very hard to say after a defeat that there are positives. We just have to try hard to keep working and keep trusting in our structure," United midfielder Tielemans told Amazon Prime. "We have to keep working, keep trusting each other and be together on this."

title: Zverev defies 'physical issues' to reach Shanghai Masters quarterfinals
body: SHANGHAI — Top-seeded Alexander Zverev toughed out two tiebreaks to beat Alexander Bublik 7-6(6), 4-6, 7-6 (1) at the Rolex Shanghai Masters on Tuesday, winning his first match since being guaranteed the year-end world No 1 ranking. The 29-year-old German will play Alex de Minaur in the quarterfinals. "Really difficult match," Zverev said. "I had some physical issues so, you know, I was maybe slower," he told the crowd. "Unfortunately, my ankle was acting up again," Zverev elaborated in an on-court interview, later adding that his decline started in the second set. "I'm starting to feel my body more, but happy to be through." Zverev, the current world No 2, was guaranteed the year-end No 1 spot after third-ranked Carlos Alcaraz lost to Zizou Bergs in Shanghai on Monday. On Tuesday, Zverev called the honor "special", saying it was a different feeling compared to winning tournaments, adding he was "looking forward" to the responsibility of owning that status. Neither player could create much trouble for his opponent in the first set, as they traded aces to hold serve. But Zverev found himself under pressure when he was forced to save a set point before making it into a tiebreak. He kept his composure as Bublik squandered three set points in a row, taking the first set with a commanding forehand at the net. That momentum was cut short when Bublik broke the German's serve in the fifth game of the second set. Despite a few clutch backhands, a somber-looking Zverev was unable to avoid tumbling into a deciding third. The players soon found themselves staring down another tiebreak, but this time Zverev raced to a 6-1 lead and closed out the match with an ace. Earlier, 56th-ranked Arthur Gea put on a convincing show to beat Jakub Mensik 7-6 (4), 6-4 in their fourth-round encounter. Mensik, ranked 15th, hit the ground trying to convert a crucial break point in the final minutes of the second set, but Gea got past his opponent with a cross-court backhand and won on his first match point. "I'm enjoying how I'm playing. I feel I'm improving all the time," said Gea, the lowest-ranked player left in the draw. Asked if he might recreate last year's "miracle" that saw Valentin Vacherot claim the title as world No 204, Gea said he would "see what happens". "I don't think it's a miracle when you work hard every day, but I hope to do the same," he said. Two days earlier, the 21-year-old Frenchman beat US Open finalist Ben Shelton, the third seed, 7-6 (5),7-6 (3) in the third round for the biggest victory of his career. Gea next faces Alejandro Davidovich Fokina, who reached the quarterfinals after beating Hubert Hurkacz 1-6, 6-3, 7-6 (6) in a dramatic tiebreak. Davidovich Fokina, ranked 26th, beat the 2023 Shanghai champion at the third time of asking, after blundering a smash and diving to the ground for a point in vain. Chinese wildcard Guo Hanyu pulled off an almighty comeback to knock out 12th-seeded Romanian Sorana Cirstea 1-6, 7-6 (6), 7-5 in the first round of the Wuhan Open on Tuesday. Guo, a doubles specialist ranked 240 in the world in singles, entered the match searching for just the third tour-level victory of her career. The 28-year-old Zhengzhou native rallied back from a set and 4-0 down against Cirstea, saved three match points in the second-set tiebreak, and erased a 3-5 deficit in the decider to complete the upset in two hours and 41 minutes. A tearful Guo later revealed to Chinese media that she was spurred on by her ailing father, who has been "seriously ill" and in hospital since July. "Knowing this actually made me feel quite helpless," said Guo. "No matter what kind of effort you make, I'm struggling recently because mentally, psychologically I always feel something. I cannot just have a happy moment on the court and enjoy the game. I will always have a kind of sorrow, so that's why I made a lot of effort today." Guo will next take on American world No 88 Katie Volynets for a place in the round of 16.

title: Changchun greets Universiade flame
body: The flame for the Changchun 2027 Winter Universiade arrived in Changchun, the capital of Northeast China's Jilin province, on Wednesday, marking a milestone in the preparations for the event, which will bring young athletes from around the world together for competitions and cultural exchanges. As of Monday, a record 3,716 athletes, coaches and officials from 63 countries and regions had registered for the games, which will be held from Jan 15 to 25. "The Winter Universiade is more than just a winter sports competition. It is an important platform for young people worldwide to engage in dialogue and deepen mutual understanding through sport, culture and academic exchange," said Wang Jiayi, vice-minister of education and vice-president of the games' organizing committee, at a State Council Information Office news conference in Beijing on Wednesday. The games will feature 97 medal events across 12 sports, with Changchun as the main competition zone and neighboring Jilin city hosting events at its ski resorts. Wang said China plans to send a delegation of more than 400 members, including 240 athletes, to the games. The team is scheduled to compete in 11 of the 12 sports, with ice hockey the only exception. The delegation will organize training camps across disciplines, and athletes will be selected based on open and fair competition, merit, and a balance between competitive ability and personal qualities. A series of test events will begin in November to assess venue operations, transportation, accommodation, equipment and emergency response. Rather than building new permanent facilities, organizers will use existing venues. Sun Jian, vice-governor of Jilin province and vice-president of the organizing committee, said that targeted upgrades would improve the refrigeration systems, ice surfaces, lighting and dehumidification equipment. The measures are expected to reduce carbon emissions by more than 4,200 metric tons, and the existing venues will be opened to the public after the games. At Wednesday's flame welcome ceremony at the Changchun History and Culture Museum, 12 representatives took part in a flame lantern relay. Short-track speed skating champion Zhou Yang handed the flame lantern to Changchun Mayor Gu Gang. Members of the flame protection team then lit the first torch of the games, named Ji Xiang. Gu passed it to Jilin Governor Hu Yuting, who used it to ignite the games cauldron. The flame was collected from Turin in Italy on Oct 8. Turin hosted the first World University Games in 1959 and has been the permanent collection site for the International University Sports Federation Games flame since 2018. Ji Xiang, which translates as "auspicious flight", draws inspiration from the clivia, Changchun's city flower. Its design incorporates a filmstrip motif to pay tribute to the city's film industry. Academic and cultural programs will complement the sporting events. The FISU World Conference, scheduled from Jan 16 to 18, will bring together more than 400 scholars, teachers and students worldwide. Under the theme "University Sport in Action: Innovation, Education and Sustainability at the Heart of the Winter Universiade", participants will discuss ice and snow sports science, balancing academic studies and athletic careers, and sustainability in university sport. Changchun, which is home to more than 50 higher education institutions and over 600,000 university students, will also host youth exchange programs, cultural exhibitions and Chinese-language activities. Organizers have selected 8,100 student volunteers from about 120,000 applicants to support the event and help visiting delegations connect with local communities. Nan Chunhua, an executive director of the organizing committee's major events department, said the flame ceremony would facilitate cultural exchanges between China and Italy, and help young people from different countries deepen their understanding of one another. Zhou Huiying in Harbin contributed to this story.

title: Athletes from 18 countries compete in World Rowing Coastal Championships
body: The 2026 World Rowing Coastal Championships concluded in Qingdao, Shandong province, on Tuesday. The three-day championships featured seven events across men's, women's, and mixed categories, including solo, double sculls, and coxed quadruple sculls, according to the event's official website. Set against the backdrop of the Golden Beach in the Qingdao West Coast New Area, athletes from 18 countries and regions competed for world titles in one of rowing's most challenging disciplines. Unlike the flat-water racing seen at the Olympic and Paralympic Games, coastal rowing takes place on open water, where athletes must contend with waves, wind, currents, and changing sea conditions. Success depends not only on fitness and power, but also on boat handling, steering, and tactical decision-making. In Qingdao, races covered a distance of over four kilometers, with the finals stretching past six kilometers. Athletes started from the beach and headed out into the Yellow Sea to navigate a series of buoy turns before racing back toward the finish. The competition was free and open to the public. A dedicated viewing area was set up near the waters off the Golden Beach.

title: Shock Alcaraz loss is Zverev's gain
body: Seven-time Grand Slam champion Carlos Alcaraz suffered a shock 7-5,7-6 (4) defeat to unseeded Belgian Zizou Bergs in the round of 32 at the Rolex Shanghai Masters on Monday, a result that also confirmed Alexander Zverev as the ATP's year-end world No 1. Fresh from defending his Japan Open title and building momentum after a wrist injury that sidelined him for nearly five months, Alcaraz never found his rhythm in a scrappy two-hour, two-minute contest. The second-seeded Spaniard joined 24-time Grand Slam champion Novak Djokovic and US Open runner-up Ben Shelton among the high-profile early casualties at the ATP Masters 1000 event. Bergs produced a composed all-court performance, thriving in the quick conditions as the 27-year-old broke Alcaraz's serve three times to clinch the biggest victory of his career. Bergs had lost their only previous meeting, falling to Alcaraz in the last 16 of last year's Japan Open, but showed no signs of intimidation as he outplayed the 23-year-old in key moments. "I often have too much respect for these guys, which is part of my culture and I'm proud of that. But it gets a little bit in the way when you have to play them," Bergs said. "The more experience you have practicing against them and playing matches, the more it becomes the new standard a little bit. "To have this moment, for me, it is a little bit of a relief. "I feel like, now, I really can win against these guys." Next up for Bergs will be Tommy Paul after the American knocked out defending champion Valentin Vacherot 6-4, 6-2. "I'm very happy how I handled the tiebreak," Bergs said. "It's never easy to get broken when you are serving for the match, but to get back in the tiebreak and play those key moments, serve big — I'm very happy with that one, especially." Alcaraz conceded that he was below his best. "I didn't play the way that I wanted to play. A lot of mistakes. I didn't find a good position on the return," Alcaraz said. "Obviously, credit to him. I would say he served really well. "But, when I got into the rhythm, when I got into the point, I made a lot of mistakes. I wasn't feeling comfortable with my shots. "So, I'm really disappointed with today's match because I didn't find the solution. I just made a lot of unforced errors." The upset also guaranteed French Open and US Open champion Zverev, 29, the ATP's year-end world No 1 ranking. "It's been a fantastic season for me winning in Paris and New York, and knowing that I will finish the year on top of the rankings is just a dream come true," Zverev said in a statement shared by the ATP Tour website. "So much work and effort have been put into achieving this goal, especially after coming back from my ankle injury," Zverev added. He suffered a career-threatening ankle injury in his French Open semifinal in 2022. Zverev will be the first German man to finish a season as the world's top-ranked player, and the oldest to lift the trophy for the top spot, set to be presented in November. Germany's Angelique Kerber and Steffi Graf have both been the year-end No 1 women's tennis players. Zverev's achievement comes in a year when the previous two players to hold the top ranking, Italy's Jannik Sinner and Alcaraz, have skipped months of competition due to injury. Sinner, the current No 1, has not competed since Wimbledon, where he beat Zverev in the final. He announced last week his season was over due to a knee injury. Alcaraz, ranked third, was sidelined for months with a wrist injury from April until the US Open. Zverev had been destined for the top from a young age, hailing from a tennis family where his mother and father both played the sport at a high level in the former Soviet Union. But he plays in the shadow of domestic violence allegations made by two former partners, which he has strenuously denied. The ATP Tour investigated one claim and found insufficient evidence to punish Zverev. Another led to a 2023 penalty order and fine from a German court, which later dropped the case after a settlement was agreed in June, 2024 — hours before he was due to play in the French Open semifinals.
